In July and August 2026, people posted a brief video as a Facebook reel and YouTube short allegedly featuring an authentic photo of a coyote standing on its hind legs and pressing a crosswalk signaling button before crossing a road.
The short video shared a story with the image claiming a wildlife camera installed along state Route 87 captured the picture outside Payson, Arizona. A sign reading "White Canyon Trailhead" appeared in the background of the image.
For example, on July 3, the Moonlit Sentences Facebook page posted (archived) the video. The Moonlit Sentences YouTube channel hosted (archived) the clip, as well.
The story claimed the coyote crossed in the crosswalk on 147 occasions, never once forgetting to press the button to signal traffic to stop:
Arizona DOT installed a wildlife camera at Route 87's pedestrian crossing outside Payson last September. Standard deer migration count. After six months, they had footage of zero deer and 147 clips of the same coyote pressing the crosswalk button with its paw at sunrise. The animal waits for the walk signal. Steps into the road. Crosses at a trot. Every single time. Biologists believe it learned by watching hikers at the adjacent trailhead. "It's not random," said the lead researcher. "That coyote understands cause and effect better than half our interns." DOT voted unanimously to keep the camera running. The coyote hasn't jaywalked once.
Another Facebook user shared a video (archived) with the image mirrored horizontally above a similar story.
One Snopes reader emailed, "Did this really happen?"
In sum, a quick investigation found the image was fake and the rumor was false. Someone used an artificial-intelligence tool to create the image, as well as possibly to write the fabricated story.
Searches of Bing, DuckDuckGo and Google found no shortage of alleged images and videos appearing to show coyotes crossing in or near crosswalks, including in Arizona. However, none of those posts showed a coyote standing on its hind legs to press a crosswalk button. Those same searches failed to locate any news media outlets, wildlife blogs or other authoritative sources reporting about the image and story users shared in the in-question videos.
We emailed a user who manages what appeared to be the originating YouTube channel to ask about the clip, as well as to inquire about the AI tools used in the creation process. We also reached out to Moonlit Sentences via Messenger to request comment and will update this article if we receive further information.
Digging into the rumor
A reverse image search located the apparent source of the AI-generated image and made-up story on the Warm Heart Chronicles YouTube channel, posted July 2, 2026, with the title "COYOTE USES CROSSWALK BUTTON EVERY MORNING AT DAWN."
The Warm Hearts Chronicles channel hosts many other YouTube shorts in the same format, with an AI-generated image in the top half of the video and a fabricated story in text below. For example, videos told made-up stories about a cat sneaking into a courtroom and cozying up next to a judge's gavel, as well as an escaped emu shutting down a Burger King drive-thru. Reverse image searches for numerous images appearing in Warm Heart Chronicles' other videos found no matches, suggesting someone used an AI tool to create brand-new, inauthentic content.
Google Maps searches confirmed no "White Canyon Trailhead" is situated near the town of Payson, as the story claimed. One search showed the White Canyon Wilderness is two hours from Payson by car, while another search found the White Rock Canyon Trailhead is about a five-hour drive.
Past plans for a wildlife safety project may have served as inspiration for the AI tool used to write the coyote story. In 2007, The Associated Press reported about an "experimental electronic 'crosswalk'" — with the word "crosswalk" surrounded by quotation marks — designed to "keep Arizona's animals and drivers safe." The project involved wildlife underpasses allowing animals to cross under roads, not traditional crosswalks at street level.
For further reading, we previously investigated another image allegedly showing a person giving a coyote a bath after mistaking the animal for a dog.

When the Indian government announced the resignation of its education minister in late July after weeks of protest, there were widespread celebrations. Students from across the country had joined the mass demonstrations led by the Cockroach Janta party amid growing resentment over repeated examination cancellations and question paper leaks.
The pressure of exams in the country has only increased in recent years. The number of student suicides rose from 8,068 in 2014, to 14,488 in 2024 – an increase of roughly 80% – according to the Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India report released by the country’s National Crime Records Bureau. After family problems, failure in examinations has been listed as the leading cause of suicides among students.
For families who say they lost their children to education system mismanagement and examination scandals, watching the protest scenes unfold on television came with mixed feelings. Some were happy that future students may be spared the same fate; others questioned why it had taken so long.
The Guardian spoke to four families about what happened to their children and how they feel today.
Anshika Pandey, 20, Delhi
Anshika Pandey, the eldest of twin sisters and four siblings, was, her father says, the calmest, quietest and most responsible member of the family. Revision books still lie neatly stacked, bags and accreditation cards hang from the nails where they were last placed. Her ambition was to be a doctor in the community where she lived, to be able to help the “poor people in need of medical care” some day.
Pandey studied for more than 12 hours every day, worked part-time at a store for nearly six hours and slept no more than five hours each night.
This year’s national eligibility cum entrance test (Neet) to gain entrance to medical training was her third attempt at becoming a doctor. After sitting the exam on 3 May, she was hopeful. But on 12 May she learned that the exam had been leaked for the second year in a row and there would be a resit.
“Anshika was deeply hurt. She had been hoping to enter college this year and was happy with the exam she had taken. Still, after cancellation, when I tried to console her, all she lamented was how could she hope to give another good exam,” says her father, Indradhar Pandey, a cab driver in Delhi.
Anshika remained calm and performed her household duties and engaged with everyone normally. But two days later, on 14 May, when everyone had left for work and her twin sister and younger brother were napping, she hanged herself.
Anshika’s dream had been to move her family, especially her siblings, from the slum where they lived. Her younger sister, Pragati, hopes to fulfil that dream and reminisces about how the two sisters had talked about it several times.
Anshika’s sketches and positive messages and mantra chants on the walls of their home, which she wrote to motivate herself, are now the memories her family is refusing to let go of.
Sufi Shaheen, 19, Delhi
Before leaving the house on the morning of 25 October 2024, Sufi Shaheen straightened her hair and put on her favourite jeans. As she left, she asked her mother for 10 rupees (8p), unlike other days when she would ask for 100. Then she headed for her joint entrance examination (Jee) lesson.
Her mother, Sultana Khatoon, asked her why she was leaving the house on an empty stomach. Shaheen replied she would be back soon. Twenty minutes later, she jumped from the seventh floor of a tutoring centre, about a mile away from her home.
It has been almost two years since she died, but Khatoon has not recovered from that day. She is being treated for severe depression and bouts of headaches.
“She was my only daughter of the four children and more like a friend. Every time I stepped out of the house, she would help me get ready. Even though she was deeply passionate about studying and becoming an engineer, she also loved dressing up and made everyone in the house do it too,” says Khatoon, as she looks through her daughter’s school photos.
Living with her parents and three brothers on her father’s modest income as a technical engineer, Shaheen had dreamed of becoming a software engineer and “excelling even more than the boys in her community”, says her mother.
A quick learner and highly motivated, Shaheen taught herself to draw and paint, and even learned to speak Japanese and Korean. But she had been stressed for several months and feared not being able to clear her second attempt at the national engineering entrance exam in January 2025.
When India’s National Testing Agency made changes to the Jee exam syllabus, Shaheen couldn’t sleep for days. She remained stressed, cried when talking to her brother and her best friend on the phone, and wrote a note to her parents in which she apologised and asked her younger brother, Masoom, to make their dreams come true.
“Almost two years later, Masoom was ranked 188th in the whole of India in his CUET [common university entrance test]. But we do not have Shaheen to celebrate this with,” says Khatoon.
Pradeep Kumar Mahich, 22, Rajasthan
“Even God will not be able to stop me from becoming a doctor this year,” were 22-year-old Pradeep Mahich’s words to his father right after his Neet exam on 3 May. This was his fourth attempt and, most importantly, he felt confident. But the announcement of the exam paper leak and resit broke his heart.
No one in the family had ever “dreamt so big”, says Pradeep’s father, Rajesh Kumar, a farmer in Rajasthan’s Sikar district. Kumar sold a large part of his farmland and took a loan of 11 lakhs (£8,600) under the farmer’s crop loan schemes.
“Sikar, the main coaching hub for Neet, is only an hour and a half from our village. My eldest daughter, Babita, who was preparing to join the police, and my son were both studying in Sikar, renting an apartment. This was his fourth year of tutoring, and the money from selling the land and the loan was slowly being consumed. I would send monthly expenses of £250 and Pradeep’s annual tutoring fees of £4,000, asking them not to worry about money and focus on his studies,” says Kumar.
“Pradeep had told me, ‘Papa, we will do a big celebration before I go to college. And one day I’ll return to serve the people of the village,’” says Kumar.
On 15 May, as he did every day, Kumar sent milk and curd to his two children on a bus that goes to Sikar; Pradeep came to pick it up at 9.30am then went home and told his sister he would help prepare lunch. But when his sister was showering, he hanged himself. She has taken a break from her studies and returned home.
Seeing students protesting on his television screen, Kumar says he is relieved that the eduction minister has gone but says there should be a proper investigation so that “no family suffers the same fate that we did”.
S Anitha, 17, Tamil Nadu
S Anitha belonged to an underprivileged lower caste, or Dalit, community from Tamil Nadu’s Ariyalur district. Born to a daily wage labourer, her mother died when she was seven, leaving her grandparents to raise her.
As a teenager, she decided she wanted to become a doctor. “At such a tender age, she was so focused that we used to feel proud of her,” says her brother, Manirathinam. “She knew what she wanted and never distracted herself with anything else. She never asked for any clothes, jewellery or food – her focus was clear and she knew the circumstances.”
She scored a perfect 100 in physics and chemistry at school and was offered a place to study aeronautical engineering at the state’s technological institute. But when she could not even meet the cut-off marks in the Neet exam, she realised that she had been studying a different syllabus.
Tamil Nadu had already criticised the national government for imposing an all-India examination – “disrupting the federal structure” – because it had a different education system. As a result, the state was exempted from Neet in 2016, but not in 2017, the year Anitha sat the exam.
When the supreme court ruled on 22 August 2017 that admissions to medical school would be based only on the Neet exam, she lost hope. On 1 September, Anitha hanged herself in her grandparents’ home. Her suicide became the subject of a public debate and led to widespread protests across the state and even in Delhi.
Her brother took part in last month’s protests in the capital and, while happy about the Indian education minister’s resignation in July, argues that all exams should become state-run, rather than by central government, as not everyone can afford the hefty tutoring fees needed to sit the Neet exam.
He now runs a free library and education centre in Anitha’s name.

Srinagar, Aug 14: Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Friday said the wounds inflicted by the 1947 Partition have not completely healed even after nearly eight decades, asserting that remembering those who suffered and lost their lives during the division of the country is a “duty towards humanity”.
Addressing a commemorative programme organised at Tagore Hall in Srinagar on the occasion of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, the LG Sinha as per the news agency—Kashmir News Observer (KNO), said the day was not merely about recalling a painful chapter of history but also about introspection, national resolve and ensuring that the tragedies of the past are never repeated.
“Today, all of us have gathered here as a community, as a nation, as a family and as a collective consciousness,” Sinha said, paying homage to those who endured immense suffering and lost their lives during Partition.
He said the sacrifices of those who suffered during Partition continue to remind the nation that the wounds caused by the division of the country have not completely healed.
“Even after eight decades of Partition, this wound has not healed completely. Even today, in the collective consciousness of India, there is a pain that has not been washed away by generations,” he said.
Sinha said history contains few examples of suffering on the scale witnessed during Partition, when millions were uprooted from their homes and communities were torn apart.
‘Remembering victims is a duty towards humanity’
The LG said Partition Horrors Remembrance Day should be an occasion to remember those whose voices were lost amid the violence and displacement of 1947.
“We will not let their pain be buried in the dust of history. Remembering them will be a duty towards humanity,” he said.
He said the memories of those who suffered must be preserved with honesty, truthfulness and compassion, describing it as the “holiest tribute” that could be paid to them.
Sinha also expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for observing August 14 as Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, saying the occasion should remain part of the collective national consciousness.
He called upon people to remember the day as more than a historical event, saying it should serve as an occasion for introspection and national resolve.
“This day is not just a page in history. It is also a day of introspection, self-reliance and national resolve,” he said.
‘New generation must know human cost of Partition’
Sinha stressed the importance of ensuring that the younger generation understands the human cost of Partition.
He said the division of the country was not merely a change in geographical boundaries but brought immense pain to families, destroyed communities and caused suffering whose memories continue to live among survivors and their descendants.
“Countless people were forced to leave their homes. Countless lives were engulfed in darkness,” he said.
The LG said society must preserve the stories of people who were uprooted from their homes and forced to rebuild their lives in unfamiliar surroundings.
“It is important for every section of society to know that during Partition, trains coming from Pakistan arrived filled with human corpses. Children, women, men and daughters were killed mercilessly,” he said.
‘Those who lost everything rebuilt their lives’
Sinha said the story of Partition was not only one of suffering but also of courage, resilience and reconstruction.
He said people who lost everything demonstrated remarkable courage, hard work and self-confidence to rebuild their lives.
“Those who had lost everything regained their lives through their courage, hard work and self-confidence,” he said, adding that many displaced families transformed the places where they settled through their perseverance.
He said refugee families brought with them their languages, cultural traditions and values, enriching the cultural fabric of the regions where they settled.
“Their struggle gives us the confidence that no matter how difficult the circumstances, the courage of the human soul can triumph over all darkness,” he said.
‘Partition had profound impact on J&K’
Referring specifically to Jammu and Kashmir, Sinha said Partition had a profound impact on the region, dividing families and displacing communities from their ancestral homes.
He said people who arrived in Jammu and Kashmir after being displaced from different parts of the subcontinent contributed significantly to the region’s social and cultural landscape.
“The Partition divided families, and many communities were displaced from their own homes,” he said.
Sinha paid tribute to those who rebuilt their lives in Jammu and Kashmir despite the hardships they had endured.
He also appreciated the J&K Cultural Department for organising programmes aimed at ensuring that the memories and lessons of Partition reach different sections of society.
‘Partition is not just an event in history’
Addressing the youth of Jammu and Kashmir, the LG said Partition should not be viewed merely as a historical event but as a legacy carrying important lessons for present and future generations.
“I would like to say to the youth of Jammu and Kashmir that Partition is not only an event in your history, but also the memory of those lakhs of families whose legacy is in your hands,” he said.
He urged young people to learn from the experiences of those who lived through Partition and ensure that the mistakes and divisions of the past are not repeated.
“You have to learn from their experiences. You have to ensure that the youth of Jammu and Kashmir never repeat those mistakes in the future,” Sinha said.
The LG called for strengthening social harmony, coexistence and national unity, urging the younger generation to build bridges of trust.
“You have to build a strong bridge of faith where walls have never been built,” he said.
Sinha said the collective vision should be to build an India and Jammu and Kashmir that are harmonious, strong and stable.
On Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, he called for a renewed commitment to peaceful coexistence, social harmony, ethical values and national unity.
“Today, on the anniversary of Partition, we must once again take an oath that we will dedicate our talents towards peaceful coexistence, social harmony and national unity,” he said—(KNO)

Congress leaders failed to function: Revanth Reddy says 21% Telangana voters face deletion under SIR
Revanth Reddy on Thursday blamed Congress leaders at various levels for failing to discharge their responsibilities fully.
Telangana could see more than 73 lakh voters drop off its electoral rolls, with Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy warning that nearly 21 per cent of votes face deletion during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
Reddy on Thursday reportedly blamed Congress leaders at various levels for failing to discharge their responsibilities fully.
During a video conference with ruling Congress leaders on the SIR process, Reddy directed in-charge ministers to hold reviews with those overseeing Parliamentary and Assembly constituencies in their respective districts and address the issues, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.
The ministers have been asked to conduct reviews across the districts over the next two days and prepare a report for every constituency, Congress sources said.
Also Read: 18 million voters in state could get deleted from rolls in SIR exercise
Reddy also instructed constituency in-charge leaders to remain in their respective constituencies for four days, identify issues related to the revision process and work to resolve them.
The chief minister warned that the party would not tolerate any failure to draw up and implement a proper action plan in line with the directions of the AICC.
He cautioned that a lack of vigilance among party leaders could cause significant political damage in the future.
Reddy further directed Congress leaders to expose what he alleged was a conspiracy by the BRS and BJP to delete votes, the sources said.
The concern comes as the number of electors in Telangana is expected to fall by more than 73 lakh following the SIR process, with enumeration forms for these voters classified as "uncollectable".
According to Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharshan Reddy's statement issued on August 11, the state had 3,38,26,448 voters in all. Of these, enumeration forms for 2,64,87,214 voters, or 78.30 per cent, had been digitised.
The remaining 73,39,234 forms, accounting for 21.70 per cent of the total, were classified as "uncollectable", he said.
House-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) as part of the SIR began in Telangana on June 25 and concluded on August 10. The draft electoral rolls are scheduled to be published on August 17.
SIR exercise updates
On the other hand, as many as 18.46% or 18 million of 97.8 million registered electors across Maharashtra are expected to be deleted from the electoral rolls in the ongoing SIR exercise.
These voters are either dead, duplicate, not traceable at the given address or shifted from there. Mumbai accounts for 29.6% of deletions, with Muslim-dominated areas such as Mankhurd, Colaba and Mumbadevi being even higher at almost 40%.
According to data released by the Election Commission (EC) on Wednesday, of the 9,78,54,049 registered voters, 7,60,98153 electors have been enumerated while the enumeration of 1,80,60,697 (18.46% of total electors) could not be completed. The deadline for completing the SIR exercise is August 17.

The best AI tools for job interview preparation include Exponent Practice, AceRound AI, Yoodli, MyInterviewAI, Interviewing.io, Big Interview, Huru AI, and Ophy AI. They offer mock interviews, role-specific questions, resume-based practice, technical prep, and detailed feedback.
AI has already changed how companies hire, right from resume shortlisting and initial assessments to interview screening. Thankfully, the same technology can also work in your favor. AI tools for job interview preparation can help you understand a role, research the company, prepare likely questions, practice mock interviews, and even point out where your answers fall short.
While mainstream AI models such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are more than capable of helping with the basics, dedicated AI interview tools take things a step further. We tested eight such tools that offer everything from resume-based interview questions and technical interview practice to video analysis, peer interviews, and detailed feedback. Here is how they work, which one you should choose, and how to get the most out of them.
If you want to skip directly to the best AI Tools use the Table of Contents below.
Table of Contents
How to Use AI to Prepare for a Job Interview
Before we get to the applications, which indeed make job interview preparation an easy affair, you must understand the importance of a solid foundation to begin with. Fortunately, this groundwork only requires leveraging existing AI tools you may already be using. After getting to know the details of the job interview, mainstream AI models, such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, and more, can be directed to put you at an advantage from the very initial phase of your preparation. Below is what you must do first.
→ Understand the Role and Generate Role-Specific Interview Questions
Most, if not all, job descriptions are little more than a pile of technical and corporate jargon, often failing to clearly state the requirements. Misaligned interview expectations may already put you in a bad spot during the interview, so you must ensure that you are well-versed with the job description. AI models can help you do so with a few prompts, but you must include a few crucial elements to get the best results. With all this, don’t forget to upload your updated resume for a tailored response.
For starters, you cannot miss out on knowing the core competencies required for the job you’re applying for. AI can help you identify the top non-negotiable technical and soft skills that the recruiter expects of you. Such attributes are often not understood by many applicants, which prevents them from brushing up on existing skills or learning the required ones. Next, your prompt must include identifying the success metrics, or the key performance indicators of the role.
Because every hiring takes place to solve a specific problem of the organization, it’s crucial to have an idea about the performance expectations the recruiter may have from you. For tech roles, it usually revolves around solving existing issues, improving existing processes, and related tasks. In contrast, non-tech roles focus on increasing client retention, establishing business relationships, and related tasks.
Lastly, you must also ask AI to groom you based on your resume. It will help you determine whether your resume aligns well with the role and whether any specific skills need to be spotlighted. AI can not only identify potential loopholes but also help you present your projects to the interviewer in the most convincing way possible. With this initial study of the role’s requirements, you can certainly answer questions and defend yourself with confidence.
→ Study About the Company
While most candidates think they know the company they’re applying to well, the truth is, not many perform a proper deep dive. It is an important part of interview preparation, as knowing the company helps you give more relevant answers instead of generic ones.
AI makes company research much easier, but don’t simply ask it to “tell me about the company.” Start with its current market position, products, competitors, recent announcements, and anything else directly relevant to the role.
Foremost, your prompt should include information about the company’s current market position. You can assist the AI model by attaching the company’s press releases, financial reports, product launch notes, public announcements, and more. Financial reports can also be used to project the company’s future trends, map future goals, and more, which are worth knowing about.
It’s also essential to understand the company’s competitors, as it can help you frame your answers to interview questions in the company’s favor. While you are unlikely to find many, you can ask the AI model to identify and propose viable solutions to the company’s publicly available problems. It can be a significant advantage when handled appropriately and also serves as a good background for obvious questions, such as “What will you bring to the table?” and “Why should we hire you?”
→ Analyze the Interviewer
If you know who will be interviewing you, publicly available professional information can help you prepare better. Their LinkedIn profile, current role, past experience, or area of expertise may give you a fair idea of which parts of your background they are more likely to focus on.
You can provide this information to an AI model and ask it to suggest questions that someone in a similar role may ask. Don’t treat those questions as predictions, though. Use them simply to broaden your preparation and identify areas you may otherwise overlook.
This information is also useful when preparing questions to ask towards the end of the interview. Relevant questions about their team, role, or experience with the company will usually come across better than generic ones.
→ Generate Behavioral, Situational, and Technical Interview Questions
A recommended way to ensure success in an interview is to prepare for the likely questions. The question set should not only include the basic ones, but also challenging ones to put you on the spot. That way, your real-world performance will be sufficient for selection. To begin with, the basics: you can ask AI models to generate common behavioral interview questions, such as “Introduce yourself” and “Why should we hire you?” “What if we don’t select you?” “What makes you fit for this role?” and the like.
The answers to the above questions will be based on your resume and cognitive ability, which is what AI models can help you with. Next, to tackle the technical questions, your prompt must instruct the AI model to fire deep-dive technical, situational, and project-based questions at you. During all this, you can rate your technical skills and promptly improve any weak areas.
Despite the discomfort, ask the AI model to generate questions from the perspective of an interviewer who is not interested in hiring you. Understand the questions, as they can prove to be great at identifying gaps in your resume, incompetencies, and more. You can also ask the AI model to question the relevance of your past experiences, push back aggressively on your answers, and more. This will only improve your chances of getting selected.
→ Practice Mock Interviews With AI Voice Mode
In case you are unaware, most mainstream AI models offer voice modes that are perfect for back-and-forth questioning, making them ideal for interview practice. It’s not surprising that merely reading the questions and thinking you can answer them won’t cut it, which is why you need a simulation of the interview. It may cause you to memorize answers instead of coming up with your own, which may result in you sounding like a teleprompter, or worse, freezing on the spot if you forget the exact answer, leaving a bad impression.
Voice mode is best used on the mobile versions of AI agents. First, you must tell the AI its persona by verbally describing it, uploading the job description, interview details, or any other supporting documents. We also recommend uploading your resume to ensure a curated interaction. Next, you must instruct it to ask all types of questions, including behavioral, technical, and situation-based.
Remember, the purpose of this mock interview is to prepare you for the worst, so take away critical lessons and improve yourself. For this, you can ask the AI model to rate your answers and provide you with detailed assessments to help you identify your weak points. Not only will it cure the interview phobia that you may have, but it will also improve your speaking skills, conversational awareness, and your ability to answer curveballs.

Useful AI Prompts for Job Interview Preparation
Mainstream AI models like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude can be surprisingly effective for interview preparation if you give them enough context. A common approach among job seekers is to provide the actual job description and resume, then have the AI conduct the interview one question at a time instead of generating a generic list of questions. Here are a few prompts worth trying.
1. Analyze the Job Description and My Resume
I am preparing for an interview for the job below. Act as an experienced hiring manager and analyze both the job description and my resume.
Identify:
The five most important skills or requirements for this role
The parts of my resume that match them best
Important requirements where my experience looks weak or unclear
Questions an interviewer is likely to ask about those gaps
Technical or industry topics I should revise
Five achievements from my resume that I should make sure to highlight
Don’t invent experience or skills that aren’t present in my resume.
Job description: [paste]
Resume: [paste/upload]
2. Conduct a Realistic Mock Interview
Act as the hiring manager interviewing me for the role below. Use my resume and the job description as your primary context.
Conduct this like a real interview. Ask only one question at a time and wait for my complete answer before asking the next one. Ask natural follow-up questions based on what I actually say instead of following a fixed list.
Include a mix of behavioral, situational, resume-based, role-specific, and technical questions where relevant.
Do not give me hints or feedback while the interview is taking place. Once the interview is finished, score my performance on answer quality, relevance, clarity, confidence, and completeness. Then identify my five biggest weaknesses and tell me how to improve each one.
Job description: [paste]
Resume: [paste/upload]
3. Give Me a Difficult Mock Interview
Act as a skeptical interviewer who isn’t yet convinced that I am the right person for this role.
Use my resume and the job description to identify weak points, career gaps, vague achievements, missing skills, questionable claims, or areas where another candidate may be stronger.
Ask me one difficult question at a time. If my answer is vague, generic, evasive, or unsupported, push back and ask a follow-up question. Don’t compliment every answer or make the interview artificially easy.
At the end, tell me which answers could hurt my chances in the real interview and show me how I could make them stronger without exaggerating my experience.
4. Build My STAR Interview Stories
Help me prepare 5 reusable stories from my career for behavioral interview questions.
Use my resume and the experiences I provide to identify strong examples involving leadership, conflict, failure, problem-solving, teamwork, initiative, and working under pressure.
For each story, organize the answer using STAR:
Situation: What was happening?
Task: What was I responsible for?
Action: What specifically did I do?
Result: What changed because of my actions?
Keep Situation and Task brief and spend more time on Action and Result. Ask me for missing details rather than inventing them. Where possible, help me quantify the result.
Finally, tell me which common behavioral interview questions each story could answer.
Excel in Interviews With These AI Tools
AI has made preparing for job interviews a lot less daunting than it used to be. For most people, mainstream AI models such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are already good enough for understanding a job description, researching a company, preparing likely questions, and improving answers.
Dedicated AI interview tools become useful when you want something closer to the real thing. Exponent Practice and Interviewing.io make more sense for technical candidates, Yoodli is particularly good for communication and behavioral practice, while MyInterviewAI works well for resume-based preparation. Big Interview helps with overall delivery, Huru AI makes quick job-specific practice easy, and Ophy AI covers the widest range of interview-preparation needs.
Whichever tool you choose, don’t stop after one mock interview. Upload your latest resume and the actual job description, complete a practice session, review where you struggled, and repeat it after fixing those areas. Two or three focused mock interviews will be far more useful than memorizing dozens of AI-generated answers.
Critique My Interview Answer
I will give you an interview question followed by my answer.
Evaluate the answer as a demanding hiring manager. First, tell me:
Whether I actually answered the question
What was convincing
What sounded vague or generic
Whether I gave enough evidence
Whether I spent too much time on irrelevant context
What follow-up question an interviewer would probably ask
If it is a behavioral question, also evaluate it using the STAR method.
Only after giving me this critique, provide a stronger version that retains my real experience and sounds natural when spoken aloud. Don’t turn it into a polished corporate script that nobody would actually say in an interview.
FAQs about AI Interview Tools
Can ChatGPT help me prepare for a job interview?
Yes. You can give ChatGPT your resume and job description and ask it to identify likely interview questions, evaluate your answers, conduct mock interviews, research the role, and point out gaps in your preparation. Voice mode makes the mock interview experience significantly more natural.
Are AI mock interviews actually useful?
They can be, especially when the AI asks follow-up questions and gives detailed feedback instead of simply generating a list of questions. They are particularly useful for repeated practice, although they shouldn't completely replace practice with another person when that is available.
Which AI interview tools are free?
Exponent Practice offers a limited number of free peer mock interviews, while Yoodli has a free tier. Huru AI provides free access to try its mock interviews, and Ophy AI offers free starting credits. The exact limits can change, so check each service before signing up.
What is the best AI interview tool for software engineers?
Interviewing.io and Exponent Practice are the strongest options on this list for software engineers. They focus much more heavily on coding, system design, algorithms, and other technical interview formats than general-purpose interview coaching tools.
Can I use AI during an actual job interview?
That depends entirely on the employer and interview rules. Some companies prohibit outside assistance during interviews and assessments. Unless the interviewer explicitly allows it, the safer approach is to use AI extensively during preparation and answer the actual interview questions yourself.
How many AI mock interviews should I practice?
There is no fixed number. Instead of repeating mock interviews endlessly, complete one, review the feedback, fix the weak areas, and try again. A few focused sessions with clear improvement between them are more useful than doing many interviews without reviewing your mistakes.

The people of picturesque Kangan are literally craving for justice! We need to know the immense importance of the Kangan to unveil the discrimination against its people.
Kangan Sub-Division, nestled in the majestic lap of the Himalayas, is among the most beautiful yet remote regions of Kashmir. Home to numerous valleys, dense forests, breathtaking landscapes, streams and fresh springs, it is further enriched by the Nallah Sindh, which originates from the high glaciers of Sonamarg and flows through the entire hinterland. This natural splendour continues to attract tourists from across the world.
Strategically located in the countryside of Ganderbal District, Kangan serves as the only gateway connecting the rest of the country with the Union Territory of Ladakh and provides the shortest route to the famous Amarnath cave. Its mountainous terrain shares boundaries with Bandipora, Srinagar and Anantnag districts. At Zero Point near Zojila, it separates the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. Internationally known destinations such as Sonamarg and Naranag, with their green meadows, alpine forests and lakes including Visan Sar and Kishan Sar, have earned the region a special place in Kashmir’s tourism map.
The sub-division is inhabited by multiple communities—Kashmiris, Gujjars, Pahadis, Dard-Sinas, Baltis, Pakhtoons, Kohistanis, and a small number of Kashmiri Pandit and Sikh families—who live together in harmony. Despite its rich cultural heritage and natural resources, Kangan remains economically and educationally backward. A large section of the population, particularly among the Gujjar, Pahadi and other tribal communities, continues to live below the poverty line.
Owing to its extensive forest cover, Kangan also serves as a seasonal home for the nomadic Bakerwal community, who migrate every year from the Jammu region with their flocks to the high-altitude pastures. Recognising these hardships, the erstwhile government had declared Kangan a backward area with the object of improving its economic, educational and infrastructural condition. Before the creation of Ganderbal District, residents of Sarbal, Nilgrar and Sonamarg had to travel nearly 250 kilometres to and fro to reach government offices and courts, often in hostile weather and under constant threat from wild animals.
Administratively, the sub-division comprises around eighty villages spread over a vast mountainous area. It has two tehsil headquarters at Kangan and Gund, three police stations at Kangan, Gund and Sonamarg, one Sub-Divisional Magistrate and one Sub-Divisional Police Officer. Its territorial jurisdiction extends from the Police Training School at Manigam to Zero Point near Ladakh and is home to nearly eighty thousand people.
Remoteness has left the region with serious infrastructural gaps. Several far-flung villages such as Kachpati, Hilpati, Kasana Patti and Badi Patti still lack proper road connectivity and electricity. Residents are often compelled to walk five to six kilometres through difficult terrain merely to reach a road. Heavy snowfall in winter further aggravates their hardships. Despite these difficulties, the people remain hardworking and resilient, most of them engaged in agriculture, livestock rearing, labour, small trade and tourism-related activities.
Coming back to the point of discrimination, the most pressing concern today among people of Kangan is the inadequate judicial infrastructure. Litigations from the area has increased manifold. Rapid development, rising land prices and expanding tourism, particularly in Sonamarg, Ganganagar and Naranag, have led to a sharp rise in civil disputes relating to land, property and commercial transactions. Criminal cases have also increased. Forest offences, including timber smuggling, are frequently reported. Road accidents on the widening Srinagar–Leh Highway have gone up, and a significant number of NDPS and POCSO cases originate from the sub-division. Yet only one court of Munsiff/Judicial Magistrate functions in the entire sub-division. The result is heavy pendency and denial of timely justice. Litigants from remote areas such as Sarbal, Nilgrar, Naranag and Hilpati are forced to travel nearly 80 kilometres to and fro to attend proceedings at Ganderbal. In harsh winters, these journeys become not only financially burdensome and physically hazardous but also life-threatening. Several residents have reportedly lost their lives in animal attacks. Poor litigants, senior citizens, women and daily-wage earners suffer the most due to repeated adjournments and long, risky travel. The maxim “Justice delayed is justice denied” accurately reflects their predicament.
It has been observed that in some cases, matters which ought to be filed before the local Munsiff Court are deliberately valued beyond its pecuniary jurisdiction so that they are taken to the district courts at Ganderbal. This practice, often resulting from lack of awareness among litigants, further denies accessible justice and increases both cost and hardship. The principle “Actus curiae neminem gravabit” reminds us that an act of the court should prejudice no one, and that courts have a duty to ensure equitable justice to rich and poor alike.
The demand for an Additional Sessions Court at Kangan is therefore not merely administrative but a constitutional necessity. A large number of cases pending at Ganderbal arise from this sub-division. The Hon’ble High Court had recently sought detailed information from the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ganderbal, regarding the volume of cases from Kangan and the existing judicial infrastructure. The required details were submitted, reinforcing the long-standing demand of the people.
The Bar Association has repeatedly represented the matter before the Law Minister, the Member of Parliament from Srinagar–Ganderbal, the local MLA and the Law Secretary, yet no tangible progress has been made. The residents of Kangan, together with the local Bar, continue to press for the creation of an Additional Sessions Judge Court. Their demand is genuine and rooted in the principle of equal access to justice. Such a court would reduce pendency, expedite disposal of cases and strengthen public confidence in the justice delivery system.
The doctrine “Ubi jus ibi remedium”—where there is a right, there is a remedy—forms the foundation of our legal system. Access to courts cannot remain confined to urban centres while remote mountain communities struggle for basic judicial facilities.
The people of Kangan have waited for decades for equitable institutional support. Their aspirations are neither excessive nor unreasonable. They seek only dignity, accessibility, equality and justice—the minimum that a democratic society owes its citizens. The time has come for the administration and policymakers to move beyond assurances and take concrete action. Recently, an Additional District Judge Court was established at Sumbal in Bandipora District, which is smaller both in area and population. That step was widely welcomed. Kangan, however, continues to wait for similar judicial empowerment for reasons that remain unexplained. Hope the injustice being faced by people of Kangan on legal front will end sooner the better!
Author is a lawyer by profession.

An Indian court has sentenced a high-profile former editor of an investigative news magazine to 10 years in prison after convicting him of raping a junior colleague, overturning his acquittal in a case that drew nationwide attention.
Tarun Tejpal, 63, the founder and former editor of Tehelka magazine, was accused of raping a journalist in the lift of a five-star hotel in the western coastal state of Goa during an event in November 2013. He was arrested and spent seven months in jail until the supreme court granted him bail.
A court in Goa acquitted Tejpal of charges including rape, sexual harassment and wrongful restraint in 2021.
The government of Goa challenged the acquittal before the Bombay high court, which set aside the trial court’s verdict and sentenced him to 10 years in jail on Thursday.
“He has been convicted to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment. He has been given two weeks’ time to surrender,” the police investigator Sunita Sawant, who led the case against Tejpal, told reporters.
The court also ordered him to pay a £3,900 fine, he said.
Tejpal, 63, said he would challenge the conviction in the supreme court.
He had initially blamed the assault on “a lapse of judgement” but later alleged the case against him was part of a vendetta by the Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) government in Goa.
“For the past 13 years, they have been pursuing me as a part of a political vendetta,” he said after conviction.
Sawant told reporters: “This is a sentence where a girl has stood up for her rights … so this judgment is very important for women who are working in any sector.”
The case emerged at a time when India’s handling of sexual assault cases was under intense scrutiny after the gang-rape and murder of a 23-year-old student on a Delhi bus in December 2012.
That attack triggered nationwide protests and international outrage, and prompted the government to strengthen the country’s rape laws.
Tejpal’s case severely damaged the authority and credibility of Tehelka, which had historically championed women’s rights and social justice.
The magazine continues to operate under new leadership, but it has failed to regain the influence it had before the 2013 case.

Former Dyson India MD Ankit Jain is working on a startup focused on building premium consumer appliances, sources told Inc42. The startup, which is currently operating in stealth, has raised pre-seed funding from Singapore-headquartered BEENEXT, the sources added. The amount raised could not be ascertained. While queries sent to BEENEXT did not elicit a response, Jain declined to comment. An ISB alumnus, Jain worked with Nestle India, Walmart, and 21st Century Fox before joining UK-based technology company Dyson in 2017. He was elevated as MD of Dyson India in 2021 to oversee the company’s expansion in the country. Last year, he was appointed MD of Dyson’s Middle East and Africa operations. He stepped down from the company in February this year. “Over these years, I built Hong Kong and Taiwan into a top 10 market, returned to India and turned around the business, and strengthened the Dyson into a brand that every customer aspired to own, and every business desired to build,” Jain said in a LinkedIn post announcing his exit from Dyson yesterday. In the same post, he added, “Time to build something new. More soon.” Jain’s startup will enter a segment that includes new-age brands such as Nester, Nuuk, Atomberg, Geek Technology, and Wonderchef. These brands are focusing on product innovation and newer designs to compete with legacy players such as Havells and Usha. Earlier this year, Nester raised around ₹19 Cr to expand its product portfolio, while Nuuk raised $4.5 Mn last year. Mumbai-based Atomberg has raised about $126.5 Mn to date from investors such as Inflexor Ventures, Trifecta Capital, Steadview Capital, and Temasek. It is now looking to raise ₹1,500 Cr to ₹2,000 Cr through an IPO. India’s household appliances market is expanding on the back of rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, growing adoption of smart appliances, and the expansion of ecommerce and retail infrastructure. The market, estimated at $22.45 Bn in 2024, is projected to reach $33.63 Bn by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 7.2% between 2025 and 2030.

The US travel industry has raised concerns that the Trump administration could expand its visa bond programme to more countries, warning that such a move could discourage international visitors and hurt the American economy.
The US Travel Association said expanding the programme beyond the 50 countries currently covered could have a significant impact on tourism and travel-related businesses.
“There are already rumblings of expanding this program to additional countries where visas are required, perhaps all countries where visas are required,” US Travel Association President Geoff Freeman told Reuters.
“That would have an extraordinarily detrimental effect on the US economy, on the travel industry,” he said.
The US Department of State this month made permanent a visa bond programme that was initially introduced as a pilot in August 2025.
Under the programme, consular officers can require certain tourist and business visa applicants from 50 designated countries to post refundable bonds of up to $20,000.
The bond can be forfeited if a traveller overstays their authorised period or violates other conditions of their immigration status.
The administration says the programme is designed to address visa overstays and concerns related to information-sharing, security vetting and document systems in countries with higher rates of visa violations.
The State Department has also said additional countries can be added to the programme with 15 days' notice.
The Trump administration said visa issuances to applicants from the countries covered by the pilot programme fell 83% during its first 10 months.
At the same time, visa overstays from those countries reportedly dropped sharply — from 45,488 in fiscal 2024 to fewer than 50 during the pilot period, according to the administration.
The countries currently covered are predominantly in Africa, with others located in Asia, the Caribbean, Central Asia and Latin America.
However, the travel industry argues that the programme could discourage legitimate travellers along with those deemed at higher risk of overstaying.
Freeman said the countries currently covered account for less than 2% of visitors to the United States, meaning the programme's direct impact is currently limited.
But he warned that the broader US travel industry is already experiencing a decline in international arrivals.
Travel from Canada has fallen 25%, while travel from Asia is reportedly at around 50% of 2019 levels, Freeman said.
Preliminary data from the National Travel and Tourism Office showed that total overseas travel to the US was down 4.3% year-to-date through June. International travel also fell 1.8% in June, despite the FIFA World Cup being held during the period.
The travel industry had hoped the World Cup would provide a major boost to international tourism and encourage policymakers to introduce measures that would make visiting the US easier.
Freeman said the weaker-than-expected visitor numbers during the tournament should instead serve as a warning against policies that could further discourage international travel.
“If we can't have year-over-year increases in travelers during the World Cup, which we didn't, what the heck are we going to do in an average September?” Freeman said.
The US Travel Association's concerns come as the administration seeks to tighten immigration controls while the tourism industry tries to attract more international visitors. An expansion of the visa bond programme could become another obstacle for travellers and further weigh on international tourism to the United States.
(With Reuters inputs)

Walmart did ban Darling from its stores, as confirmed by a company spokesperson.
Darling was not banned for buying other people's groceries, according to the company — he recorded pranks and stunts in Walmart stores, which the company deemed disruptive enough for a ban. Furthermore, a video uploaded to Darling's YouTube page in April 2025 suggests he was banned from Walmart more than a year before this claim spread.
On Aug. 11, 2026, the social media influencer and comedian Damon Darling posted a video (archived) showing an interaction with a police officer telling him he had been issued a lifetime ban from entering Walmart stores. Darling has filmed many of his videos on Walmart premises, including a series in which he pays for other shoppers' groceries or gives out money.
As the video spread on social media, other users suggested that Darling had been banned specifically because he was attempting to pay for other customers.
Snopes readers contacted us asking for more information.
We found that the claim was a mixture of true and false information. Walmart confirmed it had banned Darling from its stores. However, according to the company's statement, he was not banned for his charitable actions.
We contacted Walmart and Darling's team for this story. We spoke briefly with a Walmart spokesperson via phone and received a statement via email, but had not heard back from Darling. We will update this story if we do.
Walmart's emailed statement to Snopes read:
Helping people is part of who we are, and we are always looking at ways we can partner with others to better our communities. Over the last two years, Mr. Darling repeatedly engaged in ways that created safety concerns and customer disruptions. We have a responsibility to create a safe and respectful place to shop and work, and will continue to do so.
Snopes found that while Darling's recent content may be more wholesome in nature, some of his older videos involved pranks and skits inside Walmart stores that shoppers may have complained about. Those older videos are not available on Instagram and other short-form video platforms but are still accessible on YouTube.
For example, in a video uploaded in February 2025 titled "Walmart Shoppers Do Anything For Money," Darling asks a woman to clip one of his toenails for $100. (Interestingly, Darling is never at a Walmart during that video — he's at a Kroger.)
Reviewing Darling's YouTube page also revealed that his ban may not have been as recent as people presumed. In a very brief clip at the end of a video uploaded on April 11, 2025, titled "Walmart BANNED me for life," Darling is approached by two police officers at a Walmart in Xenia, Ohio, who inform him that he has a trespass order for "all Walmarts."
While Darling and his team did not reply to Snopes' request for comment, the content creator did discuss the ban in an Aug. 11, 2026, interview with TMZ.
"I respect their wishes. I'm at a point where I'm just going to do what they ask me and not come back and not film at their business," he said. "I don't want any problems, I don't want anyone boycotting Walmart."

Rahul Gandhi gets relief as SC quashes summons
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday set aside a Lucknow trial court’s order summoning leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi in a criminal defamation case over his remarks about VD Savarkar.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that the required sanction had not been obtained in the matter."Additional Solicitor General and advocate for complainant, in the affidavit filed by UP, submits there is no disclosure of sanction. In such view of the matter, the complaint and orders passed by magistrate stands quashed," the bench said.The defamation case stems from Rahul Gandhi’s remarks about Savarkar during a rally in Maharashtra’s Akola district on November 17, 2022, held as part of his Bharat Jodo Yatra.On April 4, 2025, the Lucknow bench of the high court said Rahul Gandhi could file a revision petition before the sessions court, holding that its intervention was not required at that stage.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha had challenged the subordinate court’s order summoning him while contesting the ongoing proceedings in the case.
Satyaki Savarkar, VD Savarkar’s grandnephew, had filed a complaint against Rahul, alleging that during a speech in London in March 2023, the Congress leader claimed that V D Savarkar had written in a book about an incident in which he and five to six friends beat up a Muslim man and that he felt happy about it.
Satyaki Savarkar claimed that no such incident took place and that VD Savarkar had never written about any such episode. He sought Rahul Gandhi’s conviction under Section 500 of the IPC and compensation under Section 357 of the CrPC.The court had already granted bail to Rahul Gandhi in the case.

Toronto – Iga Swiatek captured her first title of the season with a swift 6-2, 6-3 win against Elena Rybakina in the Canadian Open final on Thursday, giving the Pole a confidence boost heading into the U.S. Open.
It was Swiatek’s first final at the U.S. Open tune-up event, and the six-time Grand Slam champion enjoyed the Toronto crowd chanting “Iga! Iga!” throughout the match on her way to victory, with a few Polish flags in the crowd.
But Swiatek told Canadian network Sportsnet that she felt angry after the win, having faced criticism from media back home amid an inconsistent season that has seen her fail to advance beyond the quaterfinals at a Grand Slam and replace her coach.
“I think that’s the first time in my life I have something like that after a victory, but it hasn’t been easy you know,” said Swiatek. “I’m happy that I kept my composure, kept my focus, and I keep growing every month no matter what the challenges, and I’m super proud I could win this one.”
The Pole was sharp and fast on the hard court in Toronto while Kazakhstan’s Rybakina was her own enemy for much of the evening.
Rybakina, the world No. 2, was broken twice in an opening set that also saw Swiatek save two break points to take command of the match. The first set was marred by 12 unforced errors for 27-year-old Rybakina, who struggled to strike the ball cleanly.
The Australian Open champion could not weaponize her serve either, with just one ace in the match, and Swiatek broke her again in the second set to take a 3-2 lead.
Swiatek, 25, dropped the next game but closed out the final three with confidence, landing a clean strike on match point to end her title drought.
“If she plays her best game she’s probably better than everyone,” Swiatek told reporters of Rybakina after the match. “You need to use all the opportunities, you can’t let yourself make mistakes or bad decisions.”
Fatigue had finally caught up with Rybakina, who played three hours more than Swiatek at the tournament prior to their meeting on Thursday as her previous three matches went to three sets.
“I was just very tired,“ Rybakina told reporters after the match. “You could see that I wasn’t pushing with the legs enough. There was a lot of unforced errors, especially on top of the net. It was just a pure lack of concentration.”
With the Canadian title, world No. 8 Swiatek will return to the top five in the rankings.

Justin Blinder lost his job two weeks before the Covid-19 pandemic hit in 2020. To pay his rent, he turned to delivery services, riding his bicycle across New York City to deliver food. As he went, he noticed the disparities in where the food items went. Which order of Nomé sushi went where and how much people tipped.
“The city started to feel much more economically and psychologically disparate,” Blinder tells WIRED. “It really changed so much on a block-by-block level. These inequalities and demographic differences were happening in such close proximity.”
That experience has morphed into an art-project gadget called Ground Truth that Blinder hopes will raise awareness about the housing affordability crisis in New York City and beyond by making a Citi Bike—one of the ever-present ebike rental options across the city—harder to ride through places where it’s harder to live.
Blinder, a Brooklyn artist and contractor at Meta, received a $10,000 grant for the project from a Brooklyn arts organization called Idle Hands.
Ground Truth is a box that will trigger the brakes on the Lyft-owned bicycle, adding more resistance to the pedals when riding through rent-burdened neighborhoods, where people living in those areas spend more than 30 percent of their income on rent. Ride past an economically well-off block, and the bike is easier to pedal. Going past a block where rent takes the bulk of the households’ incomes can slow the bike down to a crawl.
There are two versions, one that can work on a regular bicycle and one built specifically for Citi Bikes.
The box mounts on the bike’s fork and is then attached to the front brake line. A battery-powered GPS component tracks the bike’s location. As it moves, the location is cross-referenced with household economic data from the US Census Bureau’s American Community Survey, stored on the device. When the bike passes a block the dataset says has a higher percentage of rent insecurity, the microcontroller triggers a small motor that applies the brake to add resistance, and the bike gets physically harder to pedal.
Blinder is also the creator of the Covid-inspired Pandemic Pulse, an app that used real time Covid statistics to change the brightness of your device’s screen. The screen would darken whenever data showed infections growing, and then black out briefly whenever a death was recorded. As with Ground Truth, Blinder says the goal of these projects is to help people understand large datasets in a more tactile way.
“It’s really trying to make the way we traditionally visualize a lot of big data more tangible and embodied,” he says. “Create something a bit more confrontational and try to force people to consider how they traditionally look at data.”
Blinder says the device is not a working product or something other people will be able to use. (Likely for legal reasons, as you can’t just change how a rideshare electric bicycle drives.) But he has ridden about 35 miles or so, filming the experience as Ground Truth changes its resistance in different communities.
He hopes the project will also call attention to the rising cost of renting a Citi Bike. The service has raised its prices for the past five years in a row.
“The price has just become so astronomical that it felt like this really nice connective tissue in the affordability crisis, connecting all of those different elements,” Blinder says. “It’s really thinking about how affordability changes throughout the city on a block-by-block basis and how this system could allow people to experience that.”

Jharkhand student protests began on 25 July 2026 over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC Preliminary and JSSC-CGL examinations, including allegations of OMR tampering. Led by student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, protesters have demanded cancellation of the exams and an independent CBI probe. On 10 August 2026, thousands of students marched towards the Jharkhand Assembly, where police used lathi charges and water cannons. The government has since agreed to cancel three JPSC examinations, but students continue to demand a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities. As of 14 August 2026, the protests have entered their 21st day, with Mahto continuing his hunger strike and political support for the movement growing (here, here, here, and here).
Amid this, a video is being shared on social media (here, here) claiming to show Abhijeet Dipke arriving in Jharkhand and participating in the student protests. Let’s verify the claim made in the post in this article.
Claim: The video shows CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reaching Jharkhand and participating in the student protests.
Fact: The viral video does not show Abhijeet Dipke participating in the Jharkhand student protests. It actually shows him attending a CJP demonstration at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on 6 June 2026. While Dipke has supported the Jharkhand protests, he had not travelled to Ranchi at the time of writing this article. A CJP delegation, however, visited Ranchi to support the students. Hence, the claim made in the post is Misleading.
A Google keyword search found no reports confirming that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke travelled to Jharkhand or joined the student protests. Instead, multiple reports (here, here) stated that he expressed verbal support for the protests but did not physically join them, saying he did not want to hijack the movement led by Devendra Nath Mahto. We also found reports that a CJP delegation travelled to Ranchi to support students protesting the JPSC and JSSC examinations.
We then conducted a reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video, which led us to an X post by Deccan Herald dated 06 June 2026, featuring screenshots containing the same visuals as the viral video. The post was captioned, “‘We are not afraid’: CJP founder Deepak, who is leading the movement to remove Dharmendra Pradhan, has a message for the government.”
This photo was also used in a report published by Deccan Herald on 6 June 2026. According to the report, a crowd of students, young professionals, and activists gathered at Jantar Mantar in Delhi for a CJP demonstration led by CJP founder Abhijit Dipke, who had arrived from the United States earlier that day. The photo caption reads, “Founder of CJP during the protest”
Abhijeet Dipke reposted an X post by Jharkhand student protest leader Devendra Nath Mahato on 11 August 2026. The post mentioned a video call between Mahato and Dipke, during which Dipke expressed his support for the ongoing student protests in Ranchi.
To sum up, this viral video does not show CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reaching Jharkhand or participating in the student protests.

Japan PM says Putin's visit to disputed islands 'absolutely unacceptable'
- Published
Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has criticised Vladimir Putin's first-ever visit to the disputed Kuril islands on Thursday as "absolutely unacceptable".
Russian state media reported that Putin visited Iturup, known in Japan as Etorofu, one of four islands in the Kuril chain that are claimed by Russia and Japan.
Putin's trip "has worsened Japanese sentiment towards Russia," Takaichi told reporters, maintaining the island chain was "a unique territory of [Japan] historically and under international law".
The countries have been locked in a dispute over the Kurils for decades, and it is the main reason Moscow and Tokyo did not sign a peace treaty after World War Two.
The Kuril islands sit between Hokkaido in northern Japan and Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula. Four of the southernmost islands are claimed by Japan, which calls them the Northern Territories.
They are administered by Russia. At the end of World War Two, the Soviet Union annexed the island chain and deported around 17,000 Japanese residents.
During his visit, Putin sampled fish roe and spoke to island locals, Russian state media reported.
Speaking from the prime minister's office on Thursday, Takaichi said his trip "wounds the feelings of the Japanese people" and is "incompatible with Japan's consistent position on the Northern Territories".
"I hope that the Russian side will take the gravity of this matter very seriously," she said.
Earlier that day, Japan's foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi said the islands were "inherently Japanese territory both historically and under international law, and the Government of Japan strongly protests this visit".
Over the years, attempts to resolve the territorial dispute have made little progress. Bilateral ties have also remained frosty, with Japan imposing sanctions against Russia for its invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Japan has protested against previous visits by Russian officials to the disputed islands, including Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and his predecessor Dmitry Medvedev.
The Kuril islands are a strategic area for Russia, which has beefed up its military presence on the islands over the past decade. The island of Iturup is used as its primary military air base in the region.
Last month, Chinese and Russian naval warships sailed through a strait in the Kuril islands during a joint patrol.
Russia also holds regular military drills near the islands, drawing condemnation from Japan.

A new document attempting to resuscitate a floundering global plastics treaty suggests that negotiations are trending in a less ambitious direction, a leading scientific expert said.
Talks to strike the world's first treaty addressing humanity's ever-growing tide of plastic pollution fell apart in August 2025 after opposition from oil-producing nations.
The first public document since that collapse was released quietly on the weekend, but quickly came under stinging criticism from environmental groups.
While it resembles a new draft text, chairman of the talks Julio Cordano of Chile emphasised it was "an informal reference document and does not constitute a negotiated or agreed text".
Cordano noted the document took a "balanced approach", with subjects where "views remain divergent" put into brackets.
Richard Thompson, a British marine biologist who coined the term microplastics, told AFP the document was extremely similar to the draft text that was rejected a year ago.
"If anything, it's even slightly weaker," added Thompson, a researcher at Plymouth University who has served as an independent scientific observer to the talks.
Others were more scathing.
"The text cuts the international legal effort to address plastic pollution off at the knees, delivering a text that fails not only future generations, but present ones," the Center for International Environmental Law's David Azoulay said in a statement on Monday.
Once-in-a-planet opportunity
Negotiators from 185 countries have struggled to find common ground between two broad groups.
A majority of nations have called for ambitious, legally binding measures to curb humanity's production of plastic, which is expected to triple by 2060.
However a smaller bloc of mostly oil-producing states -- including Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Russia -- have pushed back against such restrictions, seeking to focus more narrowly on waste management.
Thompson suggested that rising pressure to reduce carbon emissions was leading some oil-producers to seek "an alternative market for growth" by making plastic, which is derived from petroleum.
Research published in The Lancet last year estimates that the many health problems caused by plastic pollution costs the world $1.5 trillion a year.
Thompson also expressed concern that independent scientific observers including himself had been excluded from offering expert advice to negotiators.
"That creates unnecessary suspicion," he said.
Calling the treaty "a once-in-a-planet opportunity," Thompson said he saw "no point... in agreeing on something that is too weak to deliver."
Chairman Cordano said an updated version of the "aid to negotiations" will be prepared after the next round of informal talks in Bangkok from September 27 to 30.
Formal negotiations, hosted by the UN Environment Programme, are then scheduled for March 2027.

Won't let Punjab's peace be disturbed: Sukhbir Badal after Nihang's Kirpan attack
Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Badal said he would not allow anyone to disturb peace in Punjab, asserting that the SAD would not bow down to such attempts.
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief and former Punjab Deputy Chief Minister Sukhbir Singh Badal on Friday called the Nihang's Kirpan attack on him in Maharashtra's Nanded a "larger conspiracy" aimed at taking control of the situation in Punjab and disturbing peace in the state.
Speaking to reporters after being discharged from the hospital, Badal asserted that the attackers' ultimate goal was to seize control of Punjab's political and social landscape and disrupt communal harmony as the 2027 Assembly elections approach.
"Their mission is to take control of the situation in Punjab and disturb the peace, which, as President of Akali Dal, I will never allow. Both times they attacked me in the holiest places," Badal said.
He said the Shiromani Akali Dal was not afraid and would not bow down to those seeking to disrupt peace in Punjab.
"I have never been scared, nor am I afraid now. Shiromani Akali Dal is committed to the brotherhood and pride of Punjab. Shiromani Akali Dal can make any sacrifice, but Punjab's progress and communal and religious harmony are our top priority," he said.
Badal also said the SAD remained deeply committed to protecting Punjab's pride, brotherhood and progress. He said maintaining religious and communal harmony in the state remained the party's highest priority.
"God is with me," Badal said, adding that neither he nor the SAD would allow Punjab's peace to be disturbed.
Badal underwent surgery lasting about 90 minutes after a member of the Nihang order attacked him with a Kirpan inside Gurdwara Mata Sahib Devan Ji Mugat on the outskirts of Maharashtra's Nanded town on Thursday. Doctors treating him said he was stable and out of danger.
"The surgery lasted for an hour and a half. There was a tendon injury, and he had a sharp penetrating wound. His tendon was repaired. The plastic surgeon also repaired his ulnar artery nerve. He is out of danger," a doctor at Yashosai Hospital said.
Badal suffered a wound of around five centimetres on his right forearm, Nanded District Collector Rahul Kardele said. A police officer who was also injured while protecting Badal remained stable and out of danger, the District Collector said.
Badal was rushed to Yashosai Hospital after the attack, where doctors operated on him. He was discharged on Friday and was likely to be flown to Punjab in the afternoon, according to an official.
The attack came after Badal escaped an attempt on his life at the entrance of the Golden Temple in December 2024. Visuals after Thursday's attack showed him walking inside the hospital building with a cloth wrapped around his right hand.
According to police, the accused, Jaspal Singh, attacked Badal inside the gurdwara. Police have yet to establish why Singh attacked the SAD chief.
Singh, aged between 60 and 62, holds commerce and law degrees and is based in Pune with his family. He had worked as a sewadar or volunteer at the gurdwara for the past two years and was staying alone in Nanded.
In connection with the attack, the Mudkhed police station registered a case against Jaspal Singh under Section 307 for attempt to murder, Section 353 for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of duty, and Sections 4/25 of the Arms Act. The accused will be produced before a court today.
Singh was also booked under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for attempt to murder, voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means, and voluntarily causing grievous hurt to a public servant to deter them from performing their duty.

Australia vs Bangladesh: Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century leaves tourists in charge in Darwin
Bangladesh assume 153-run lead at stumps on day two of first Test against Australia; Tanzid Hasan's patient 101 off 197 balls anchors dominant first innings with the bat from tourists as Australia feel the heat in Darwin
Friday 14 August 2026 10:41, UK
Tanzid Hasan posted his maiden century in just his second Test to help guide Bangladesh to 351-6 at stumps on Friday and into a commanding position over Australia after two days of the Top End series opener in Darwin.
Tanzid raised his hundred with a single off Nathan Lyon from 188 deliveries but, after a patient and resilient innings, added just one more run before lofting a ball from the veteran Australian spinner to Mitchell Starc at long-off soon after.
He shared two big and important partnerships to set the No 9-ranked Bangladesh on course for a sizeable first-innings lead, combining with Mominul Haque (49) in a 102-run second-wicket stand and adding 93 with skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto for the third.

Shanto went on to score 84 from 126 deliveries before becoming one of three wickets to fall in a four-over period soon after Australia took the second new ball.
Bangladesh resumed on Friday at 96-1, 102 runs behind in the first innings after dismissing Australia for 198, and finished day two with a 153-run lead and four wickets in hand.
In their first Test on Australian soil since 2003, the Bangladesh players were just as disciplined with the bat as they were with the ball on the opening day.
Mehidy Hassan Miraz (32) and Hasan Mahmud (13) shared an unbroken 43-run partnership for the seventh wicket to get Bangladesh to stumps in the kind of position few expected ahead of the series.
The reunion of Australia's so-called Big Four, pacemen Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, alongside veteran off-spinner Nathan Lyon, has so far been blunted with the visiting batters frustrating Australia in the warm, tropical conditions in the Northern Territory capital.
Seamer Starc was involved in a heated exchange with Bangladesh batter Miraz after the pair nearly collided during the bowler's follow-through.
"It's my follow-through not your follow-through, get off the wicket!" Starc said, before the umpires separated the two players.
The two-Test Top End series begins a demanding 12-month schedule for Australia that will feature 20 Test matches, including tours of South Africa, India and England.
