Quick Answer
This guide covers 45+ WhatsApp tips and tricks, including usernames, privacy tools, AI summaries, message translation, custom lists, HD photo sharing, chat locks, passkeys, call scheduling, PDF tools, stickers, reminders, and more.
WhatsApp is on a roll lately, adding plenty of features to its platform. While some of the features are very useful, others are cluttering the core experience and blurring the line that separates it from other Meta apps.
WhatsApp is still the most used communication app around the world, with billions of users exchanging messages every single day. Most people only utilize the basic features of WhatsApp.
WhatsApp is also feature-packed like other applications, with plenty of useful features that can come in handy while using the app. Most of these useful features are buried inside settings, which most people are generally not aware of.
In this guide, I will walk you through a full collection of the best WhatsApp tips and tricks to help you get the absolute most out of the app. Most of these features are free to use, and Meta isn’t limiting these features to their paid WhatsApp subscription. So, with that in mind, let’s get started.
Table of Contents
Create and Share a WhatsApp Username Without Revealing Your Phone Number
WhatsApp finally rolls out usernames, where you can now create and share them with others to contact you without revealing your phone number. Up until now, if anybody wants to contact you through WhatsApp or you want to contact anyone, you need the user’s phone number.
Phone number sharing isn’t a feasible option since it can be used for other purposes, not just for contacting on WhatsApp. Additionally, more people are hesitant about sharing their phone number with strangers.
But with the new WhatsApp usernames, you can hide your phone number and share just your username as your WhatsApp contact.WhatsApp also allows you to edit your username and add a second layer of connection privacy, including a six-digit code. If you enable this, users must enter it to text you on WhatsApp.
In regions like India, WhatsApp is currently limiting the rollout of usernames. This is because they can be impersonated, as usernames do not reveal any personal details.
Usernames have already started rolling out on WhatsApp. If you haven’t reserved one, you can follow the guide below and do it as soon as possible. Please remember that you will still be required to link your phone number to WhatsApp to get a username.
Annotate PDFs Directly in WhatsApp Without Downloading Them
Annotating PDFs is the most stressful job that many of us go through frequently. Even to make basic edits, you need a separate application like Adobe Acrobat, or you have to depend on browsers’ built-in annotation tools, which sometimes also require you to go through multiple steps.
With the introduction of basic annotation tools on WhatsApp, the need for basic annotation tools is solved if you use WhatsApp on the web or desktop.
WhatsApp recently announced basic PDF annotation tools for WhatsApp Web and desktop, which are powered by Adobe Acrobat. It lets you annotate PDFs without downloading them if you received them on WhatsApp.You can also annotate PDFs outside WhatsApp by directly uploading the file by messaging yourself, and performing basic annotation tasks such as highlighting text, underlining, and drawing.
You can then download or share it with others. The only downside is that WhatsApp currently only offers the basic tools, which include drawing, highlighting, underlining, and a strikethrough tool. It would be nice if WhatsApp also added the ability to quickly add a signature.
To do that, open WhatsApp on the desktop and follow these steps:
Step 1: Tap on the message icon and tap on “Message yourself”.
Step 2: Upload the PDF and then tap on it.
Step 3: Tap on “Edit PDF” from the top menu.
From there, you can edit the document. Once you are done, you can directly share it on WhatsApp or click on the download option to download it locally.
Use Two WhatsApp Accounts on One Phone
WhatsApp now allows you to use multiple accounts (maximum of two) in a single app. Previously, the reliable solution was installing the WhatsApp Business app to use multiple accounts, but WhatsApp has made it easy. You can now switch between accounts and link another WhatsApp just by using a second phone number. Here is how to add a second WhatsApp account.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and tap the horizontal menu in the top right corner.
Step 2: Tap on the settings option.
Step 3: Tap on the plus icon next to your profile name.
Step 4: Tap on Add New WhatsApp Account
Step 5: Agree to the privacy policies and enter your phone number. Enter your phone number, enter the OTP, and enter your secondary verification PIN if you have set it; that’s it. To switch between profiles, follow the same steps: click on the plus icon next to your profile name, and select the other account to switch.
Review and Strengthen Your Privacy With Privacy Checkup
WhatsApp privacy controls can be confusing for beginners. There are a lot of settings to control, such as who can see your profile picture, last seen, and default message timer, and who can add you to groups, who can message you, and much more.
WhatsApp Privacy Checkup is designed to help you control these settings very easily. You get a single dashboard with a detailed, step-by-step guide that lets you manage those settings easily. Here is how you can use it:
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and tap on the three-dot menu, then tap on Settings
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on the Privacy option
Step 3: Scroll down and tap on the Privacy Checkup option, and from here you can go through each step to control all your WhatsApp privacy settings.
Read Voice Messages With Automatic Transcriptions
WhatsApp voice chats are great. You can simply record your voice and send a note, and also receive them.
There are times when you receive a personal voice message, or you are in a place where you cannot play your voice note. In those cases, you can simply transcribe the voice note and read it instead of listening. You can long-press and tap on Transcribe to generate a translated text of the voice note. If you don’t see this option, you should first enable it from the settings.
Step 1: You need to enable transcription first. To do that, open WhatsApp, tap on the three-dot menu in the top right corner, and tap on Settings.
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on Chats
Step 3: Now scroll down again and tap on the option that says Voice message transcripts.
Step 4: Once done transcribing chats, open a chat and long-press on any voice message, tap on the three-dot menu at the top, and tap on the Transcribe option.
Summarize Unread WhatsApp Messages Instantly
Hundreds of messages in groups can quickly pile up, especially those office communications that you must read, no matter what. Fortunately, there is a nifty feature on WhatsApp that reads all your unread messages and summarizes them for you.
This is done through WhatsApp Meta AI, where WhatsApp says this is a part of private processing where it doesn’t read your messages and all the processing happens locally on your device. This is also not enabled by default. You should go to Settings, and then Chats, and then enable Meta Private Processing.
Once you are done, you can open any group with unread messages and tap on the Unread Messages pill at the top, and you get a quick summary. This also works for individual chats.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to any individual or group chat with unread messages
Step 2: Tap on the unread messages pill at the top, and that’s it. WhatsApp will create a summary for you.
Step 3: Currently, it is only available in limited countries.
Translate WhatsApp Messages Automatically
This can be useful, especially if you have a contact in another country who doesn’t speak your language.
WhatsApp comes with a native translation feature where you can long-press a message and translate it into any language you want. The most useful feature is the ability to auto-translate all incoming messages from a specific contact. And it also supports two-way translation, which means the messages you are sending in return will also be translated into their languages. This is one of the useful features on WhatsApp that avoids the long wait barrier.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to any chat you want to translate. Long-press on the message and click on the three-dot menu in the top right corner of the screen
Step 2: From here, tap on the language you want to translate from and choose the language you want to translate to. Remember that you need to download the language.
Step 3: If you want to translate all messages from the chat, enable the option that says translate all new messages in this chat.
Add a Personal Role Tag to WhatsApp Groups
There are times when, in WhatsApp groups, I have been mistaken for someone else. Fortunately, if you are in multiple groups and this happens to you, you can add your personal role inside groups so that users can see it and identify you before text. This also helps them to understand what your role.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to the group profile you want to add the tag.
Step 2: Tap on Add Member Tag, add your member tag, and click on Save.
Turn Any Word Into a WhatsApp Sticker
More than 50% of my conversations with anyone are through WhatsApp stickers. And with my friends, I just communicate through stickers and rarely use text.
The best part is that WhatsApp also allows you to import stickers from third-party apps, and you can also create your own stickers now. While WhatsApp allows you to create your own stickers from your images, if you want to quickly highlight your text through stickers, you can go to the sticker tab and type your message, and your text is converted into a sticker. It is not only faster, but so seamless that you can just generate text-to-sticker in just a few steps.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to any chat.
Step 2: Tap on the stickers icon and tap on the search bar inside the stickers section.
Step 3: Now start typing the text; WhatsApp automatically displays stickers with the typed text. You can simply tap on it to send.
Organize Chats and Groups With Custom Lists
WhatsApp lists are the most underrated feature, in my opinion. For those who are not aware, lists are like chat filters that currently appear on top of your WhatsApp chats and underneath the search button. You can create up to 52 lists.
The best use of lists is that they separate your personal chats from your work and also make a separate list for all your groups to categorize them. For instance, you can divide the WhatsApp chats or groups into friends or work.
The two biggest advantages I personally find are that WhatsApp’s “All Chats” view is generally cluttered with unwanted advertisements, especially in India. You can quickly switch to any list for a clean interface and see only messages from the chats you wish.
Here is how to create WhatsApp lists:
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and, if you see lists, swipe left and tap on it; if you don’t see lists by default, drag/swipe down from the chats to reveal them.
Step 2: You can give it a name and tap on Add people or groups. If you have the Plus subscription, you can also apply a theme and ringtone for all messages coming from this list.
Step 3: Next, add users or groups you want to add to the list and tap on Done. That’s it; your list will be created. You can just tap on the list to visit.
Set Custom Notification Sounds for Important Chats
WhatsApp notification sounds are handy; they quickly let you know that you have received a message. If you are at work and focused, but you also don’t want to miss critical notifications, you can set separate notification tones for specific chats. So, whenever you receive a notification from the chat, instead of the default notification, WhatsApp uses the notification you have set to notify you.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to any chat for the group profile and tap on the Notification option
Step 2: In the notification settings, tap on the Notification tone and set a custom notification tone.
Add WhatsApp Chats and Groups to Your Home Screen
If you use WhatsApp for group or other personal communication that you often go to, you can directly add those specific chats or groups to the home screen and launch them directly from there.
Step 1: Open any chat on WhatsApp and tap on the three-dot menu at the top, then tap on More
Step 2: From here, tap on the Add Shortcut option, and this contact will be added to your home screen.
Rewrite and Polish Messages With WhatsApp AI
Turning on Meta AI Private Processing also enables AI writing tools, which let you rephrase your messages. Well, this isn’t a feature that I use for personal messages, since I always believe they should be real and authentic instead of AI-written.
Since WhatsApp is also used for professional communication, there are times when you need to fix spelling mistakes or format a message in a specific way. Moreover, these AI writing tools are also available directly inside keyboards, so you can utilize them there.
Send HD Photos by Default
WhatsApp recently got an option that lets users share high-quality images instead of compressing them. Previously, to do that, I recommended sharing images as document files. This is no longer required. Whenever you are sharing images, you can just select the HD option to send them in high definition.
If you want that high quality as a default and don’t want to select high definition for every single image you send, you can enable it from the settings.
Archive Marketing Messages Without Blocking Senders
I live in India, and here WhatsApp has become the main communication platform, even for business and marketing messages. There is no way to stop them, and the worst part is that if you try to block them, the company will appear on your feed with another number.
The most effective method is archiving those messages instead of blocking them. When you archive a message, WhatsApp hides it from your message chats and creates a separate archive page, which you can tap on top of your messages.
These will be hidden by default, even if you are on the main chat list. You will also not get notified of messages received from these chats, but you can easily view them if there is anything important.
Step 1: Go to the messages or content you want to block and long-press on it
Step 2: Click on the archive option at the top
Step 3: To view archived messages, tap on the archive option in the All Chats option, and you will be taken to all archived messages.
Edit Sent WhatsApp Messages
WhatsApp now allows you to edit a message once you send it. Currently, it allows you to edit the message within 15 minutes. If you accidentally share the message, you can simply long-press it, tap on the horizontal bar in the top-right corner, and tap on Edit to edit your message.
Remember that WhatsApp displays an “Edited” text to let the other user know, but it won’t display the previous version. If it’s more than 15 minutes, you can use the “Delete for Everyone” option.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to the chat
Step 2: Send a message to edit. Long-press the message and tap on the pencil icon in the top toolbar
Step 3: Now edit the message and tap on the right option. That’s it. Remember that it only appears under 15 min
Protect Your WhatsApp Account With Two-Factor Authentication
Our post “How to Recover Hacked WhatsApp Account” still receives a lot of messages from people asking how to get back their accounts.
If you don’t want to be one of them, I highly recommend you enable two-factor authentication for your WhatsApp account. For those who are unfamiliar, two-factor authentication is an extra step that you need to go through when you are logging into WhatsApp. Along with the number OTP verification, you need to enter a six-digit PIN code to log in to your account.
So, even if hackers manage to sign in with your phone number through OTP, they still need to enter the two-factor authentication PIN to gain access to your account.
This is the easiest and most reliable way to add extra security that prevents your WhatsApp account from being hacked, unless a hacker also has access to that PIN. Remember that once you create a PIN, do not share it with others. And also remember the PIN, as WhatsApp frequently asks you to enter the PIN to secure your account.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and tap on the three-dot menu at the top, then tap on Settings
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on the Account option
Step 3: Now scroll down and tap on Two-factor authentication
Step 4: Now tap on Turn on and follow the on-screen instructions to set a 6-digit unique secondary authentication code. Do not forget this PIN; it also asks to set a recovery email, so don’t skip this step.
Sign In Faster With WhatsApp Passkeys
WhatsApp also supports passkeys. For those who are unaware, passkeys are a new login method that uses your device credentials to log in to any account without using an email, password, or any other verification methods.
It simply uses your device verification identity, such as your fingerprint or Face ID, to verify it’s you and log in to your account.WhatsApp also supports passkeys, which let you log in to your WhatsApp account using your device or Face ID if you reinstall the app.
While passkeys make it easy to sign in without requiring you to remember a password or enter an OTP, if you lose your device or if the passkeys are accidentally deleted, it is a hassle to recover your account.
I wouldn’t recommend using passkeys for WhatsApp because, unless you frequently log out of your WhatsApp account, there is really no need to set them up.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and tap on the three-dot menu at the top, then tap on Settings
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on the Account option
Step 3: Scroll down and tap on the passkeys
Step 4: Tap on Create passkey, and then you can use your device credentials to create passkeys on WhatsApp.
Create Personal Event Reminders in WhatsApp
WhatsApp allows you to create events and set reminders for those events in WhatsApp groups. However, you can also create a group with you as the only active member to create events and use it as a reminder.
It doesn’t support recurring reminders. You can only set reminders a minimum of 15 minutes before and a maximum of one day before. It can be very helpful if you have any private events planned and you don’t use a separate reminders app.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and tap on the search option, and from here tap on the message yourself
Step 2: Once you’re in, tap on the attachment icon and tap on the events icon
Step 3: From here, you can add an event. You can also add a reminder about the event, which is very useful.
Manage a To-Do List With Meta AI
Meta AI wasn’t the best when compared to ChatGPT or Gemini, but it is available directly inside WhatsApp. The best part is, since these tasks are directly linked to your account, even if you switch devices, you can get access to them on the same WhatsApp account.
Since it is an AI application, the possibilities are endless. You can create a to-do list and ask Meta AI to use other productivity principles (such as the Pareto principle) to create actionable tasks. You can also ask it to postpone tasks, mark them as completed, and much more. Even more useful, it supports context, so you can ask follow-up questions or inquire about your previous tasks.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and click on the Meta AI icon on top of the message icon on WhatsApp
Step 2: Now enter the prompt. You can use our to-do list actionable prompts to create actionable results,
Scan Documents and Send Them as PDFs
WhatsApp now comes with support for an inbuilt scanner, where you can scan documents, convert them directly into PDFs, and share them with others. Combined with the PDF annotation tools, it can replace your existing document scanner app.
Document scanner is also available for both Android and iPhone. It also supports auto capture, where you can point your camera at the documents and it automatically captures and converts them into a PDF with correct edges.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and tap on the attachments icon
Step 2: Tap on the documents option and tap on Scan Documents
Step 3: From here, you can point out your camera to scan the document and capture as many pages as you want, and once done, tap on the right option
Step 4: The document will be saved as a pdf and you can share it with any contact. You can also message yourself to save it for yourself on your WhatsApp chats.
Start a Group Voice Chat Without Calling Everyone
WhatsApp now has a Clubhouse-like voice chat feature for groups, where you can have a voice chat with the members of the group without making a call.
To do that, open any group and swipe up from the bottom; a new option appears as “Start Chat.” Tap on it, and the other group members will be notified so they can join, and you can have real-time conversations. It also supports options where you can mute, exit the group, or exit the voice chat anytime.
Call Only Selected Members of a WhatsApp Group
WhatsApp group calls can be annoying, especially if they aren’t meant for you. Most people in a WhatsApp group are not aware of this feature, and automatically group call everyone. WhatsApp allows you to call specific people in the group instead of everyone:
Step 1: Tap on the phone or video icon at the top.
Step 2: Click on the right arrow.
Step 3: Select only the people you want to call, and then start the call.
Post Multiple Photos in One WhatsApp Status
Instagram layout is the most popular feature, but most people aren’t aware that WhatsApp also offers a similar layout feature. It allows you to select six pictures and create a status with a similar collage layout, just like Instagram; it’s best for sharing multiple images in a single status instead of six different statuses for each image. Here is how
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to the status tab and click on Add New Status
Step 2: Tap on the layout option
Step 3: From here, you can add up to 6 images. Select all images and tap on the right option
Step 4: From here, you can select different layouts, and once finished, tap on Done to share the status in the new collage layout
Create and Share a Direct WhatsApp Link
WhatsApp usernames are a handy feature, but still, if you want to choose to share your phone number with the closest ones, you can directly share your WhatsApp direct link instead of just sharing your phone number.
Instead of users manually using the phone number, they can simply tap on the link and message you directly on WhatsApp.WhatsApp again doesn’t offer you the ability to share your profile link.
You can use this web link to do that: you can type wa.me/ and enter your phone number with the country code. You can also use third-party tools, but this is very easy to remember, rather than going through multiple steps to create a single WhatsApp link.
Step 1: To create a WhatsApp link, go to any chat and enter this link: wa.me/91xxxxxxxxx and add your number in the place of x. If it doesn’t load as a link, you can add https:// before wa.me. Example: https://wa.me/91994848493994
Silence Spam Calls From Unknown Numbers
If your phone number is exposed, anyone with that phone number can directly call or message you on WhatsApp. To prevent unknown and spam calls, WhatsApp has introduced a “Silence Unknown Calls” feature, where it automatically mutes calls from new contacts.
It is very effective at blocking calls from unknown numbers, especially those spammy marketing calls. Here is how to enable this setting on WhatsApp.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and click on the three-dot menu and tap on Settings
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on the Privacy option
Step 3: Scroll down again and tap on Calls
Step 4: From here, turn on the option that says Silence unknown callers
Automatically Delete Messages in New Chats With a Timer
WhatsApp now allows you to set a default disappearing timer for all new chats. When this is enabled, all new chats, unless you have modified individual chats, will disappear after the time you have set.
This is especially useful for temporary communications without cluttering your messaging in chats. Remember that these messages will be automatically deleted after a certain time. If any message is important to you, you need to manually turn off the disappearing messages option for that content. If it is turned on, you can also save important messages by long-pressing on them.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and click on the three-dot menu, then tap on the option that says Settings
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on Privacy
Step 3: Scroll down again and tap on the default message timer
Step 4: Here you can see the time for the message timer
Schedule WhatsApp Calls in Advance
A surprise voice call from friends is always joyful. There are times we miss a call from them, or they miss a call from you because of busy schedules.
To avoid this problem, WhatsApp is now allowing you to schedule WhatsApp calls so that everyone knows the call time in advance. This is especially useful if you are making time for a discussion, having a group chat with your friends, or holding a professional meeting.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to the Calls tab
Step 2: At the top, tap on the option that says Schedule
Step 3: Now enter the call details and tap on the Send button
Step 4: Next, you can add all contacts to the calls list and tap on the right icon, and it’s done; other users will receive a scheduled call notification.
Find All WhatsApp Desktop Attachments in One Place
WhatsApp is slowly adding features to make it a more reliable option, including using it standalone without depending on your phone. The recent addition is the ability to view all WhatsApp media in a single place.
Plus, since the media is available directly on the desktop, it is easy to manage. It lets you view all the media files,including images, docs, and links, in a single place, and also allows you to manage and delete them.
Step 1: Open web.whatsapp.com and tap on the media icon on top of your profile. From here, you can manage all your media at once. You can use media, docs, and links to switch, and also a filter option for filters.
Receive Only Important WhatsApp Group Notifications
Another drawback of being in groups and muting notifications is the increased chance of missing an important message from the group.
WhatsApp has a new setting called “Notify for You,” which only sends you an important notification for the messages that contain your name, are replies to your messages, or are other relevant messages.
Since WhatsApp doesn’t use AI here, it does not notify you based on the message contents, but it does use those parameters and notifies you for relevant messages. This is better than muting all group notifications if you don’t want to get distracted.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp, open the group, and tap on the group name at the top to see its group profile
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on the notification option
Step 3: Now scroll down again and tap on the Notify for option
Step 4: Now, from here you can select the option that says Highlights.
Check How Many Group Members Are Online
WhatsApp now also shows how many people are currently online in the group. This way, you can decide whether to share an important message at a specific time or not.
Step 1: Open any group, and underneath the main group name inside the chats, you can see how many people are online.
Find a Forgotten WhatsApp Group Through a Contact
If you accidentally forget the group name. You can easily find it out using the person’s name you remember in the group. There is an easy way to find out: you can go to the person’s profile and see which groups you both belong to.
Remember that WhatsApp only shares if you both belong as active members of that specific group. If you accidentally exited the group and forgot the group name, it won’t work.
Step 1: Open the chat and tap on the profile icon at the top to go to its profile info
Step 2: Scroll down and tap the Groups in Common section, and from here you can see all the groups that you and the person are a part of. You can tap on the group to visit the group directly from here
Turn Videos Into Animated WhatsApp Stickers
Animated stickers are currently more popular and more engaging than static stickers. You can also create these short animated stickers from short videos.
Using the native sticker maker, you can select any short video, and it converts that video into an animated sticker.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to the chats and tap on the stickers option
Step 2: Tap on the Create Sticker option
Step 3: Now select the video from the media, trim it, and tap on Done
Step 4: That’s it. WhatsApp will create a sticker and ask you to share it. You can also download the stickers, and once the sticker is sent, you can also tap on the sticker and add it to your favorites.
Create a WhatsApp Group Without Adding Members
Creating a WhatsApp group with only you as an active member can be very useful. You can use those groups as a personal chat to store your important information.
To create a group, you had to add at least one member to it before it could be created in the past. WhatsApp has changed the rules: you can create a group, even an empty group, without adding members.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and tap on the message yourself icon
Step 2: Now tap on the new group option
Step 3: Now, on the screen, it asks you to select the group members; You can skip this step by clicking on the next icon in the bottom right corner of the screen
Step 4: Now you can enter the group name and tap on the right icon, and that’s it.
Keep Important Chats Easy to Find With WhatsApp Lists
The free version of WhatsApp allows you to pin up to three chats for free. If that becomes limited for you, you can use the chat list to organize them. The idea of the pinned chats is to make them visible and easy to find.
When adding them to a list, you should add three chats for a better experience. This ensures you get similar results without cluttering the screen. WhatsApp also allows you to reorder the list and add the list as a favorite. This way, you can keep the most important chat lists easily accessible.
I have already shared how to create lists on WhatsApp. You can create a new list and name it Pinned and add chats or groups to the list, long-press on the pinned list, and reorder and move it to first or second for easy access.
Send Live Photos and Motion Photos on WhatsApp
Live and motion photos are becoming the trend lately, especially on iPhones, where it is enabled by default. Now, if you want to share these live and motion photos, WhatsApp natively supports this feature, so you can directly share them with others.
Mention an Entire WhatsApp Group in Your Status
You can use WhatsApp group mention to notify group members and update without sharing the message in the group. While adding a status, you can simply mention a group name, and all the group members are notified and can also reshare the same status.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and create a new status, and at the bottom, tap on the @ icon
Step 2: From here, select the group, and all group members will be notified about the status update
Stop Others From Exporting Your Chats With Advanced Chat Privacy
Advanced chat privacy is especially useful if you want to prevent the other user from exporting your chats and saving media directly into their gallery. When you enable advanced chat privacy, which is available inside each individual chat’s settings, you can prevent the entire chat export and prevent users from automatically saving media into the gallery.
I would highly advise you to use this feature, especially if you are having a chat with a stranger for the first time.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to any chat and tap on the chat and go to the chat’s profile
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on the advanced chat privacy option, and on the screen, enable the option that says advanced chat privacy
Hide the Locked Chats Folder With a Secret Code
WhatsApp now lets you hide specific chats completely with a lock.
Locked chats are visible by default when the user swipes down. You can completely hide the Locked Chats folder and reveal it only when entering the code into the WhatsApp search.
This can be very useful, especially since the code is unique. Even if the user tries to guess your code, it won’t display the locked chats folder on WhatsApp.
Step 1: Scroll down and go to your locked chats, and inside the locked chats, tap on the three-dot menu, then tap on the horizontal menu, and tap on the locked chat settings
Step 2: Now enable the option that says hide locked chats
Step 3: If you have set the PIN, it asks you to set the secret code and set the PIN, and finally enable the option
Step 4: Now, to view your locked chats, enter the secret code, and the locked chat will appear.
Hide Your IP Address During WhatsApp Calls
If you use WhatsApp for making unknown calls, then it’s better to hide your IP address completely.WhatsApp directly allows you to hide your IP address from the settings, letting the WhatsApp servers make the call from their IP address instead of exposing your IP address completely.
This way, the other person could not misuse the information about your approximate location or your internet service provider, which is usually exposed if your IP is exposed. And in the same way, you can also disable the web link previews so that WhatsApp will not contact the linked website to generate its preview, which can also expose your IP address to that specific site.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp settings
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on Privacy
Step 3: Tap on the advanced option and enable the options that say Block unknown account message and Protect IP address in calls.
Mark Every WhatsApp Message as Read
If you are someone who doesn’t like having the message notification numbers on your chats, there is an easy way to mark all messages as read. Simply tap on the settings in the top right corner of the screen, and then tap on “Read all.”
Remember that doing so will also mark the messages you explicitly ignored as read.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and tap on the horizontal menu in the top right corner
Step 2: From here, tap on the Read all messages button.
Search WhatsApp Messages by Date
WhatsApp also allows you to search messages on specific dates instead of relying on keywords. You can go to the chat you want to find and tap on its profile. Tap on the search icon, and then tap on the calendar icon. From there, you can select a specific time frame and search all the messages.
Step 1: Go to any chat or group message and tap on the chat name and go to the user or group profile
Step 2: Now tap on the search option
Step 3: Now, in the search bar, tap on the calendar icon and enter the dates you want to search for the messages.
Keep Media From Specific Chats Out of Your Gallery
You can prevent WhatsApp media from automatically downloading and showing up in your device gallery. You can disable these two settings. If you want to stop media from a specific user only, you can go to their profile, tap on Media Visibility, and select “No” from there.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and go to the chat or group profile you want to stop media from saving
Step 2: Scroll down, tap on Media Visibility, and select and turn it off.
Move the Text Cursor Precisely With the Spacebar
It is hard to tap the exact position and edit the text on small screens like mobile phones. If you are using WhatsApp, you can use the spacebar to move the cursor right and left.
This way, you can quickly place the cursor exactly in the position you want and quickly edit the text. Although it sounds like a lot of effort compared to tapping in the exact position, I found this much easier than the standard method.
Step 1: Enter the message, and now long-press the space bar and move the cursor from right to left.
Appear Offline on WhatsApp While Using Other Apps
Using the WhatsApp proxy, you can disable internet access to WhatsApp by simply going to the settings and changing the proxy to 1.1.1.1 or 1.0.0.0. You can also disable internet access for WhatsApp to appear offline. While using the rest of the apps fine.
Step 1: Open WhatsApp and click on the three-dot menu at the top, and tap on Settings
Step 2: Scroll down and tap on Storage and Data
Step 3: Tap on the proxy option
Step 4: Now tap on the Set Up Proxy option
Step 5: and in the proxy host enter this number: 1.1.1.1 and tap on the done button, this way you can appear offline using proxy.
Read Deleted WhatsApp Messages With Notification History
WhatsApp allows users to delete messages both for themselves and for the sender. If you enable notification history on your device, you can easily read them. To do this, go to Settings and enable notification history. This currently only works on Android phones and on the web through third-party extensions like WA Web Plus.
On Android, if you enable notification history, it keeps track of all the notifications you have received, including the notification content for messages that the other user deleted later. On the web, you can simply install the extension and tap on “Restore Deleted Messages,” and it will display all the deleted messages for you.
The only catch is that you will only be able to see future deleted messages, not the ones that were deleted before you enabled this feature.
Step 1: These steps can vary depending on your Android phone. You can use the main search bar and simply tap on Notification history and enable it
Step 2: Open settings and tap on Notifications
Step 3: Scroll down, tap on More settings
Step 4: Scroll down again and tap on Notification history
Step 5: now in the next screen turn on the feature that says notification history, that’s it, here all your notification history will be saved.
Read WhatsApp Messages Without Appearing Online
Sometimes you want to read your messages but don’t want to appear online. There is an easy way, like turning off your internet connection. Your last seen status will still be updated automatically if you open WhatsApp.
To see your WhatsApp messages without opening the app, you can add the WhatsApp chat widget to your phone’s home screen and enlarge it. This displays all your chats and the messages you have received, allowing you to read them without ever opening WhatsApp.
Step 1: On your phone, long-press the home page and select the Widgets option
Step 2: Search for the WhatsApp widget, select the 4×2 WhatsApp message widget, and add it to the home screen. Drag it to make it big
Step 3: From here, you can see all the messages appear from WhatsApp here.
Get More Out of WhatsApp With These Tips and Tricks
So, those are an extensive list of tips and tricks on WhatsApp. Since WhatsApp rolls out new features every month, we keep this list updated with the latest tips and tricks.
If you use WhatsApp regularly, you can bookmark our post for more new tips. If you have any issues while enabling these tips and tricks, you can comment below, and I will help you. Some tips are only available in certain regions while few are only available in the latest versions, you can update WhatsApp to the latest version to get all these features.

Nearly one in three Indian women aged 15-49 years is now overweight or obese, up from one in four women five years ago, according to data released by the Central government. The latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) found that 30.7% of women aged 15-49 years were overweight or obese in 2023-24, compared with 24% in NFHS-5 (2019-21). Among men in the same age group, the proportion rose from 22.9% to 27.3%.
Speaking of the rising incidence of lifestyle-related disorders on fertility and pregnancy, which is prompting greater attention to health before conception, doctors and health practitioners are now increasingly focusing on the period before pregnancy, arguing that identifying and addressing health risks in both prospective parents could improve reproductive and pregnancy outcomes.
“The concept is not new to Ayurveda. The traditional system has described garbhadana samskara, a pre-conception regimen aimed at preparing prospective parents physically and mentally before conception. The approach is now being offered as a structured programme at the SDM College of Ayurveda and Hospital in Udupi, Karnataka, which has been providing pre-conception counselling and care to couples from different parts of south India,’’ Mamatha K.V., principal and senior obstetrician at the institution, said.
Describing this approach as the “conscious preparation for conception”, Dr. Mamatha said that the process involves assessment of the health of both partners, along with advice on diet, lifestyle, and other factors that may influence reproductive health. Pre-conception consultations can provide an opportunity to identify risks, review medicines, address nutritional deficiencies and encourage healthier lifestyles before pregnancy.
In Ayurveda, conception is described through four factors — ritu, the appropriate fertile period; kshetra, a healthy reproductive tract; beeja, the healthy sperm and ovum; and ambu, adequate nourishment. “Interventions are tailored around these factors, with dietary and lifestyle changes and, where considered appropriate, traditional therapies,’’ Shreyashri Suvarna, a physician at the hospital, said, adding that traditional interventions need to be individualised and clinically supervised.

Trump slaps a 100 percent tariff on heavy and 'sensitive' drones
The move will force operators to find other suppliers or settle for models with lesser capabilities.
President Trump has imposed tariffs up to 100 percent on drones that are "particularly sensitive" for national security, the White House announced. The move will force operators to find other suppliers or settle for models with lesser capabilities than the Chinese drones that dominate the market in the US.
The White House will impose a 100 percent tariff on drones over 25kg (55 pounds), or those equipped with docking stations or thermal imaging capabilities. Those include commercial models from DJI and others used for operations like power line inspection, crop spraying and search and rescue. Drones under 25kg will be hit with a 25 percent tariff, and a 15 percent levy will be applied to models from the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan, provided their components are primarily made in those countries. UK drones will see a 10 percent tariff hit.
The aim with the tariffs, the White House stated, was to strengthen national security and encourage "on-shoring" of drone components. To the latter end, the government is creating incentive programs for US companies that make new investments in the manufacturing drones and drone components. The move will also close a loophole that allowed companies to buy components from China and assemble them in the US, an expert told The Financial Post.
The new White House tariffs follow a recent FCC move to ban sales of LiDAR-equipped drones it had previously approved, including models from DJI currently available in the US. The new tariffs appear unrelated to a current US ban on new DJI drones, cameras, microphones and other consumer products.
As with the manufacturing of smartphones and other high-tech products, China is leaps ahead of the US and any other country when it comes to drones. DJI's models, for example, are so technologically superior to any other brand that they're virtually irreplaceable in the market. They can't easily be built in the US for the same reason smartphones can't: America lacks the localized supply chains, specialized factories, unique engineering knowledge and large-scale skilled labor pools found in China.

Sicily's busiest travel hub, Catania Airport, will remain closed until early Friday morning as Mount Etna, Europe's most active volcano, continues to erupt, according to a Bloomberg report. The ongoing volcanic activity, which has affected over 1,350 flights over the past week, has severely disrupted summer travel to the popular island destination.
According to the latest post, the airport extended the halt on passenger flights through 8 a.m. Friday. It was earlier said all takeoffs and landings would remain suspended at the island hub through at least 2 a.m.
According to the airport operator, Società Aeroporto Catania, and local reporting by La Repubblica, the closures have caused widespread travel chaos, with about 1,000 flights cancelled and another 350 rerouted to other facilities between Aug. 6 and Aug. 12.
More than 100,000 passengers are estimated to have been affected, La Repubblica reported.
With Catania closed for the majority of the week, flights have been diverted to other Sicilian airports, including Palermo, Trapani, and Comiso. This sudden shift in logistics has created severe challenges for travellers on the ground. Some passengers have been forced to sleep at the airport, while many have had to rely heavily on buses and trains to reach their destinations.
A severe shortage of available rental cars has also caused local transportation prices to skyrocket, according to a Bloomberg report.
Ryanair, a dominant carrier at Catania, said passengers should expect heavy delays, cancellations and diversions on Thursday. While Wizz Air, EasyJet and Ita Airways are among the other carriers active at the hub in southeast Sicily.
EasyJet said it cancelled its one return flight from London Gatwick on Thursday, while Wizz said it’s been trying to divert planes.
However, Comiso has also been affected by Etna’s plumes, and Palermo has become crowded, “so there are some flights which we have to cancel, unfortunately.”
Società Aeroporto Catania, which also operates Comiso airport, said it is coordinating with other airports and authorities to manage the Etna ash emergency.
Mount Etna’s frequent eruptions have often hindered flights at Catania, its volcanic ash coats everything — from airport runways to patios and swimming pools. Aircraft flying by the volcanic ash risk fouling sensitive engine components.
Tourism accounts for about 4.2% of Sicily’s economy, according to a Unicredit report in March, with an estimated 22.5 million visitors last year. Small-business lobby Confartigianato said separately that tourism, restaurants and hotels were expected to create about 20,000 jobs in the third quarter.
According to preliminary estimates compiled by industry group Assoesercenti, four days of disruption would affect between €13 million ($15 million) and €24 million in tourist spending.
The island needs a permanent, centralised planning body to coordinate between airports, airlines and other businesses to ease the impact of Etna’s eruptions, said Salvo Politino, Assoesercenti’s president.
“We can’t stop the Etna, but we can prepare,” Politino said. “Above all, we can prevent every natural disaster from turning into an economic and image emergency for Sicily.”
(With Bloomberg inputs)

A Canadian payment giant is being sold to U.S. private equity. Is your digital privacy at risk?
Moneris handles roughly 1 in 3 payment transactions across Canada
A payment processing company responsible for approximately one in three payment transactions across Canada will soon be owned by an American private equity firm.
The Royal Bank of Canada and Bank of Montreal announced earlier this week they would be selling jointly owned Moneris, one of Canada's largest commerce solutions providers, to Francisco Partners for $2 billion.
So far, it's been positive for both RBC and BMO, with the companies' shares jumping after the deal's announcement. RBC expects to gain about $475 million from the sale after tax, and BMO $600 million.
However, some industry analysts are raising concerns the move could have negative repercussions for Canada's digital sovereignty amid the country's ongoing trade war with the U.S.
Wide-reaching implications
Broadly speaking, digital sovereignty refers to the power of a country, or individual, to retain control over its own digital assets.
In September, AI Minister Evan Solomon said that Canada needs to create a sovereign digital economy that is "free from coercion."
That same month, dozens of experts and academics penned an open letter urging Prime Minister Mark Carney to swiftly "defend Canada's digital sovereignty" and protect the country from the whims of the Trump administration.
It's a sentiment Sharon Polsky, president of the Privacy and Access Council of Canada, shares.
"Canadians should be concerned because this is their information," she said.
"We're now going to have what has been a Canadian data-processing company that has access to everybody's purchasing habits ... available to other governments."
Thousands of businesses in Canada use Moneris. The processor services more than 325,000 points of commerce and processes more than $5 billion in transactions every year, according to a press release from the company.
Polsky said the deal means Canadians' data could be available, not only to foreign governments, but foreign law enforcement agencies.
She gave an example of U.S. border agents potentially checking an individual's transaction history before allowing them to enter the country.
"Will you be stopped at the border because your purchase records indicate that you bought something with THC?" she said, referring to a chemical compound found in cannabis, which remains illegal in the U.S. under federal jurisdiction.
"It's possible these days, much more possible than ever before."
Transaction data as leverage?
That the deal is happening as the countries grapple with a trade war only heightens Polsky's concerns.
"It's easy to foresee that the rich data that comes from millions of Canadians' purchases could easily be leveraged to inform trade negotiations," said Polsky, who has advised corporations and governments for more than 30 years on privacy and access matters.
Colin Deacon, an Independent Canadian senator, is also concerned about how the U.S. government could use Canadians' data.
"[Data] under force and under request from the U.S. government could be then shared on an individual basis," said Deacon during an interview with CBC's Power and Politics.
"There's a number of ways in which [U.S. President Donald Trump] has absolute control over services that Canadians rely on every day."
Both BMO and RBC pointed to press releases announcing the deal, refusing to provide further comment when contacted by CBC News.
"As ownership transitions to FP, Moneris's commitment to serving Canadian businesses will remain unchanged," read a separate press release from Moneris.
Privacy legislation in the works
Canada's legislation meant to protect digital privacy isn't where it needs to be, according to Polsky, who said this comes at Canadians' "collective peril."
"Canada isn't ready," she said.
Polsky argues there's a clear outcome if a company based in Canada is compelled by the U.S. to supply data as a result of this deal.
"If the choice is either to comply with the American law or go to jail, or comply with Canadian legislation that really is nowhere near as stringent … it's a no-brainer. They will comply with the American legislation."
The Canadian government has taken steps to address digital sovereignty. In June, the government introduced Bill C-36, the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act.
It proposes a major overhaul of Canada's private sector privacy framework, updating language to establish privacy as a "fundamental right" and replace parts of the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA), which sets out rules for how businesses, including tech, airlines and banks, collect and use customers' data.
The bill also requires companies to conduct a "privacy impact assessment" before transferring personal data outside of Canada.
At the time, government officials said the legislation would cover any company that has a "substantial connection" to Canada.
But Polsky said C-36, and the Liberals' other attempts to update Canada's digital privacy laws, only "dance around the issues."
"They don't really speak to data being retained in Canada as a matter of national security or as a matter of data sovereignty," she said.
Bill C-36 represents the Liberal government's third attempt to update privacy regulations, following failed attempts in 2020 and 2023. It underwent its first reading in June, but has a number of steps to go before becoming law.
Meanwhile, the sale of Moneris still requires regulatory approvals, including clearance under the Competition Act, and is expected to close by the end of the banks' fiscal first quarter in 2027.
Where does that leave Canada?
"Behind the eight ball," said Polsky.
"[Canada is] trying to look tough, but we have a ways to go."

Veterinary doc dies by suicide after being cheated of ₹1.40cr in UP: Police
Gorakhpur veterinary doctor, 52, allegedly dies by suicide days after filing FIR alleging ₹1.40 crore fraud by a woman and her associates.
A 52-year-old veterinary doctor allegedly died by suicide in his apartment in Gorakhpur’s Rajendra Nagar on Thursday morning, six days after he lodged an FIR alleging that a woman and her associates had cheated him of ₹1.40 crore, police said.
Police said the woman and her father have already been arrested in connection with the alleged fraud case, while the circumstances surrounding the doctor’s death are being investigated.
Gorakhnath’s Circle Officer Ravi Kumar Singh said the deceased was posted as a veterinary doctor in neighbouring Maharajganj district. He lived with his wife, who is also a veterinary doctor, and their two children in Rajendra Nagar.
Police officers said they received information through PRV-112 around 9:40 am that a person had fallen from the apartment. The man was taken to a nearby private hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.
The deceased had lodged an FIR at AIIMS police station on August 5, alleging a ₹1.40-crore fraud involving a woman holding a PhD, her father (a railway official), her husband and others.
Singh said the circumstances surrounding the death of the veterinary doctor are being investigated and developments related to the alleged cheating case are also being examined as part of the probe.
Police have taken the body into custody and initiated further legal proceedings.

Kurukshetra man stabbed to death in Germany, had planned to visit home on Diwali
The motive of the murder could not be immediately ascertained.
A 25-year-old man from Kurukshetra was allegedly stabbed to death in Frankfurt, Germany, by a group of three men on Tuesday, his family said on Thursday.
The motive of the murder is yet to be ascertained. The man, who was identified as Vishu Sharma from Mahadev Mohalla, last spoke to his family on Monday.
Vishu’s father Neeraj Sharma, who works at a jewellery shop, said: "We did not hear from him on Tuesday and learnt of his death on Wednesday morning from his roommate Gaurav. He said Vishu had injuries on his body. After some time, Gaurav switched off his phone. Then, we sent one of our relatives living in Germany to the hospital to identify him.”
He added: “I was told that on Tuesday, a group of three men called Vishu outside his room and stabbed him to death, after which Gaurav rushed my son to the hospital.”
Vishu’s family said he had left for Portugal in November 2022 and was due to come home this Diwali. They added that they spent approximately ₹20 lakh and sold a plot of land to send him to Portugal in search of a good job.
After a year, Vishu shifted to France, where he underwent six months of military training and served in the French Army for about a year. After leaving the French Army, he moved to Germany and began working in the delivery sector, his family said.
Neeraj said his son had formed a team of delivery workers who worked under his supervision.
The deceased’s sister Noni said she had already sent a Rakhi for her brother and Vishu had promised to give her a ring on Raksha Bandhan.
Vishu's uncle and former councillor Nitin Bhardwaj said the family is now completing formalities to bring his mortal remains to India.

"Look at that subtle off-white coloring. The tasteful thickness of it. Oh my God, it even has a watermark."
Credit:
Aurich Lawson | American Psycho (Lions Gate Films)
Anthropic has revealed that it will soon watermark content that is processed (not just generated!) by any of its models. In a support article, Anthropic explained that it was rolling out machine-readable watermarks to comply with the European Union’s AI Act, which requires all AI system providers to watermark AI-generated or manipulated audio, image, text, and video outputs. The law applies to any AI model released after August 2 and provides a grace period until December 2026 for providers to update previously released models.
Anthropic confirmed that moving forward, all new models offered globally—not just in the EU—will mark AI-generated content “from day one.” Text outputs will “carry embedded watermarks,” invisible to the user, and other “generated files will include digitally signed provenance metadata where supported,” Anthropic said.
Notably, Anthropic is deploying a “nuke it from orbit” approach, applying the watermarks to all processed content where supported, even though the EU does not require it for cases where an AI system performs “an assistive function for standard editing” (the guidance’s own example is grammar correction), or where it doesn’t “substantially alter” the user’s text or its meaning.
A watermark applied at the model level can’t tell wholesale generation from a comma fix, so Claude may end up stamping exactly the content the law was written to leave alone. How thoroughly it truly watermarks will not be known until Anthropic releases a detection tool that can be tested. The company said that it plans to eventually share details about how to detect marks in order to offer technical support that the EU’s law requires.
Anthropic also noted that the watermarks won’t work on “some platforms or features” that don’t support them. For non-text content, Anthropic will use the C2PA metadata approach to record provenance.
Easy to get around, easy to misunderstand
The approach described by the EU and implemented by Anthropic is unfortunately trivially easy for bad actors to bypass, while potentially punishing users who trust the system to accurately label their outputs. Text watermarks work by biasing the model’s word choices in a pattern spread across the entire document, only detectable in aggregate by the right tool. The catch is that “invisible” can also mean the model occasionally trades the best word for a slightly worse one, just to keep the signal intact.
Anthropic noted that those marks “will travel with the text when it’s copied and pasted elsewhere, and may persist through some editing.” But if watermarked text is pasted into another chatbot system that edits the text, the watermark could be destroyed. With image and video content, screenshotting/recording or using any decent metadata editing tool will suffice to remove this information, too. And once Anthropic tells the world how to identify these watermarks, building a system to remove them would be trivial.
Further, the potential for misinterpretation seems high; the watermark is not particularly informative. Anthropic explained that a “detected mark provides a signal that content was processed by Claude, but is not fully conclusive.” The only real message the mark sends is that “the content may have been processed by Claude,” Anthropic said, and the mark may even appear on content that was not generated by Claude.
On top of this, you have the general public, who may not grasp the difference between processed text and wholly generated text. If the system watermarks human-authored text simply because it was edited in a workflow that touches Claude, suddenly it carries the same denotation as wholly generated text does. And all of this in a system where the “lack of a detected mark doesn’t mean the content wasn’t AI-generated or processed,” Anthropic said.
Claude may label more AI content than required
To its credit, Anthropic acknowledges that it may be marking some content that the AI Act does not require to be labeled: “People often use Claude to proofread, translate, summarize, or convert files. The output can carry a Claude mark even if the underlying ideas, text, or data originated from another source.” So, despite being explicitly exempted by the law, Claude will mark any editing work done on original writing.
If the watermarks become a catch-all for any Claude use, from spellchecks to complete rewrites, Anthropic’s solution will likely frustrate users by going further than necessary to label content in ways that could inadvertently muddle provenance. A teacher or professor, for instance, should not interpret this watermark signal as anything beyond “AI touched this,” but it is easy to imagine they will. After all, what is the point of a watermark that cannot differentiate between light editing and wholly generated text?
The matter becomes even murkier when we turn to another section of the EU AI Act, 50(4), which addresses how those publishing such text must explicitly label content. Under their labeling regime, wholly generated AI text does not require a label in most instances. AI-written novel? No label. Marketing copy generated by AI? Nope. But if the text is meant to “inform the public on matters of public interest,” you have to label it unless a human reviews it editorially (meaning, the editor is known and accountable). So, we have a strange situation where, on the model level, it’s “watermark all the things,” but on the public disclosure front, it’s “you don’t need to label this AI text if Joe looked at it.”
Ars reached out to Anthropic to see if there’s a timeline for details on detection to be released or results from any testing the company can share assessing the likelihood for false negatives or positives. We also asked if Anthropic could address how its watermarks may conflict with standard editing and other exemptions from the AI Act, but Anthropic did not immediately respond.
The fun is just starting
In the EU, transparency requirements are meant to ensure AI tools like Claude don’t upset “the integrity and trust in the information ecosystem, raising new risks of misinformation and manipulation at scale, fraud, impersonation, and consumer deception.” One EU support article forecasted that the obligations would be the “primary compliance challenge” for many AI firms.
“People should know when they are interacting with AI or exposed to AI-generated content,” the European Commission’s guidelines said. “This will help them make informed decisions, calibrate their trust and reliance on AI, and avoid misinformation or deception.” Still, it’s hard to square this with the fact that a wholly generated article on a matter of public interest gets a watermark, but not a reader-facing label, if an editor properly reviews it.
AI firms like Anthropic are best positioned to develop watermarking solutions, the EU expects, since AI moves fast and there will be an ongoing “need for new methods and techniques to trace origin of information.”
But that largely leaves the societal value of such marks up to tech firms to decide, with the EU only stipulating that “techniques and methods should be sufficiently reliable, interoperable, effective and robust as far as this is technically feasible.”
In its post, Anthropic said it plans to continue working on its watermarks and detection methods that meet the EU’s demands. If Claude’s labels fail, the AI Act carries steep penalties for violations, including fines up to 15 million euros, or 3 percent of a company’s worldwide annual revenue.
Ars Editor-in-Chief Ken Fisher contributed to this report.
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

Phoebe Bridgers tends to stand out in a crowd, and not just because of her celebrity or natural star quality, but because of the hair; other women around L.A. may go for the platinum blonde look, but not quite that platinum. So it was fairly easy to pick her out for the entirety of the 10 minutes or so she spent skating with her fans Tuesday night at the Moonlight Rollerway in Glendale, California. But she was easy to spot, in this instance, from head to toe, as she was the only skater on the floor in brightly strobing light-up skates… an equipment option that the Moonlight was not able to offer any of the couple hundred fans who joined her. At this very action-packed listening party for her. The beaming Bridgers had earned the right to wear skates that special; this was not her first rodeo, clearly, when it came to making dozens of laps around a rink and outpacing a crowd.
As one fan commented on Reddit after the YouTube-sponsored event: “She was skating right with everyone, and if you could match her speed then you could say hello, but she is FAST so it may have been a bit difficult.”
Popular on Variety
Of all the albums that could be previewed with an evening out at an old-school roller rink, “Lost Weekend,” the singer’s long-awaited third solo album, would not jump out as the most obvious candidate… even if Bridgers is hell on wheels, as it turns out. The 16-track record has as many hushed passages as you’d expect from a Bridgers album, and it does not sound at all designed to inspire extended bouts of cardiovascular activity. And Bridgers did use the word “weird” in characterizing the juxtaposition when she spoke about her reasons for hosting the event there in a brief Q&A she did with fans at the event after the skating wound down. Yet, for her, it was an aspiration being realized.
“I’ve had this idea forever” she said to the crowd of about 200 sitting on the rink’s floor. “I always thought it would be cool to do like a Grouper Moonlight night… You always kind of skate to ABBA or something. I thought it would be interesting to listen to sad and slow songs and skate.”
She’s had the same impulse at amusement parks, she pointed out. “I always thought about that at Six Flags,” she said saying that, while waiting in line for rides, she’d wished she could take the typical revved-up theme-park soundtrack and “catapult it somewhere” and replace it with music that was “30 bpm or something.” To her mind, slowcore and Tatsu might be the perfect fit.
Anyway, Bridgers’ promotional campaign for “Lost Weekend” has been unusual enough that a rollerskating listening party almost — almost — doesn’t stand out as that unusual. ,The singer-songwriter first began teasing “Lost Weekend” a few months ago with a series of pop-up gigs in small towns and middle American cities, places like Roswell, New Mexico, before the album was announced or even widely known to be in production. WIth the moment of release finally at hand, her team booked planetariums across the country and even in Europe for Spotify-sponsored listening parties where fans could experience the album for the first time this week with trippy visuals, if sore necks — a way of getting “Lost” in space, sort of. (And no phones allowed, as with virtually every pre-release event for the record.)
Another fairy unusual element of the promo campaign: no interviews. She hasn’t done a single one for “Lost Weekend,” so the roughly six minutes she spent answering fan questions at the Moonlight Rollerway may have constituted as much talking about the record as she plans to do, at least right away. Bridgers didn’t exactly talk anyone’s ear off in her quick, friendly response to the fan queries, but the answers still offered glimpses of insight as to where she’s coming from with this album and its attendant cycle of events and touring.
One of the first hands that went up from the crowd was to ask whether she’d been inspired by any other artistic media while making the record. “Well, there’s a movie called ‘Lost Weekend’ that’s about alcoholics’ kind of fugue state,” she said, referencing the harrowing 1945 Billy Wilder drama that some of her younger fans might not know. “That probably goes well (with the album), unfortunately.” She hesitated while trying to think of another example, then did come up with a musical reference point. “Do you guys know ‘The Lemon of Pink’ by the Books?” (Not everyone did — the Books are not exactly a household name — but some murmured their assent for the 2003 album, which has a strong following as a seminal indie-oughts cult record.)
Someone else wondered: Why the small-town pop-up tour? And what was her takeaway from what seemed like it might be an experiment? “I just wanted everything with this album to feel like it’s happening in real life,” she explained. “Like, I didn’t live through a time where I didn’t find out about something on the internet. Even cool pop-up shows and stuff, it was all kind of phone-based. So I just liked the idea of plastering a small town (with flyers)… It was so fun.” Her answer to the second part of the question: “The biggest takeaway was like, yeah, the internet’s not real. It’s all a fake,” she said, to laughter.
Another question: How did she decide it was time to come back? — the unspoken assumption being that six years between albums counts as a lot, even if there was a monumental Boygenius album and tour in between that came to feel like a very viable separate career.
“I mean, I didn’t love all parts of being away,” she said, with a chuckle, noting that while she knew she needed to pull away for a bit, it wasn’t necessarily a plan to wait this long. “I kept booking studio time and then putting it off… and booking studio time and putting it off, and putting it off… I really wanted to be making something,” she allowed, but the album was not yet ready to take shape. “So I just started going in and then taking six months off and then going (back). So this album took forever. Which is great!,” she added, harboring no regrets about leaving anyone in suspense.
After those and a few other questions, it was time for her to sign the big stack of posters commemorating the event. Prior to the Q&A, meanwhile, Bridgers premiered a rough cut of the second video for the album, for the song “I Can’t Wait,” which she said was nearly done, except for some drone footage that was shot during this very event that will be folded in.
There was a no-phones policy, but there were also no NDAs, so fans freely shared their experiences on Reddit and other forums after the event… including their impressions about Phoebe Bridgers being as good at skating as at music.
“I ate shit 3 times out there and got a sore ass today,” wrote one fan. “It was even more embarrassing because she was shredding around the rink.”
Others spoke of approaching Bo Burnham or Bridgers’ mother, Jamie Bridgers, for off-rink convos. But when it came to meeting the star attraction, some found her intimidating, despite her best efforts to be a fairly unassuming skatergrl. Some agonized afterward about not having found the right words when they made it to the front of the signing line. One spoke of becoming tongue-tied, but “I was towards the end of the line and it had been almost 2 hours at that point. She probably did appreciate our efficiency lol!!” Another wrote, “I just said ‘Yo this album fucking rips,’ and she laughed and said thanks.” One person who admitted being unable to do anything but blurt out their name said that as they left the signing table, Bridgers politely called out, “It was nice to meet you.”
What will she do for an encore? That’s obvious: do sold-out two- and three-nighters at the nation’s biggest arenas, like the three-night stand she has upcoming at the Intuit Dome Oct. 30-31 and Nov. 1. Between now and then, there is much parsing of the 16-track album’s rich content to be done, with millions of words of formal and informal think-pieces to come. (Read Variety‘s own take on the album here.)
While fans who didn’t make it to the Moonlight Rollerway may have a lingering case of FOMO, it may still be possible to replicate the feel that Bridgers was going for, as she’s longed to marry slow sounds with frenetic action. You could go to Magic Mountain and do X2 while listening to “Lost Weekend” on earbuds; we can now be certain the author would approve.

Luma Reader by TechPP turns long webpages into short, animated paragraphs for a cleaner and more engaging reading experience. It removes distractions, saves highlights, remembers your progress, supports dark mode and font controls, and works on desktop and mobile browsers.
There are hundreds of reader apps and extensions available for free. But the idea behind our extension is not just offering a clean and distraction-free reading experience but also making reading text more immersive, especially in an era where people prefer watching videos over reading text.
Thanks to short-form content, especially platforms like YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels, users’ attention span has reduced drastically. It is even affecting the longer video format, and text is currently the least preferred way of consumption for most people.
Short-form text is currently the trending format, thanks to AI tools; however, similar to short videos, most short-form answers don’t offer the full context, depth, and meaning of the information.
So we built a simple motion-reader extension to enhance the reading experience. The extension not only strips all unwanted content from the web page but also displays animated text, making the reading experience more immersive and visually appealing while keeping it short and simple. It strips out long text from any webpage and converts it into short, interactive, readable content.
The extension is also free to download. You can get it from here, and at the end of this post is a detailed guide on how to install and use it on Google Chrome on desktop and mobile browsers. The process is very similar for other browsers too.
Here are five reasons why you should use our Luma Reader by TechPP extension:
Table of Contents
Read With Short Motion Paragraphs
The biggest reason why people prefer short-form content is that it is easy to grasp and also visually appealing. That’s not the case with text. Most websites, especially news and blog sites, still use long reading paragraphs, which are immediately a red flag for many people.
In addition to that, many webpages have other distracting elements that can hinder the user’s reading experience. To make text easy to read, our extension visually presents the text, strips out all the unwanted content on a web page, and gives you simple, short paragraphs.
Even if the web page consists of longer paragraphs, our extension converts text into smaller interactive sentences (max of two or three) to make it easy to read.
Once you finish reading the current sentences, you can swipe up for the new text, or swipe down if you want to read the previous text. This way, you won’t feel overwhelmed by the amount of text.
This short and simple, guided, interactive reading experience is significantly better and less mentally demanding, and breaks the information into bits that are easier to read.
Highlight and Save Important Points
We also added the ability to highlight text and save it permanently. It works just like any other text annotation tool: you can simply long-press on any text and click the highlight option. All the text highlights will be permanently saved on your browser storage unless you manually delete the browser data. You can revisit these highlights at any time.
Continue Reading Where You Left Off
The USP of our Luma Reader extension is the ability to read from where you left off. Most reader extensions just strip the web elements. Since ours uses a unique approach of showing the small text in motion animations, it is important to let users read where they left off instead of scrolling from the beginning. Our extension remembers where you left off and resumes from there.
Read Comfortably With Dark Mode
Most people prefer reading text in dark mode. If you are one of them, our Luma Reader extension supports dark mode too. You can simply enable it from the top toolbar. You can also adjust different levels based on your preference.
Customize the Font Size
To give the best reader experience, we are also letting you adjust the font size and keeping it default to sans serif, which is known to offer the best reading experience. You can also increase or decrease the text, change how many paragraphs should appear at once, and more.
Use It on Mobile and Desktop
This extension is built for both mobile and desktop, and it works on all browsers. Since most users read text on mobiles, we put extra effort into optimizing it for mobile use. Not a lot of mobile browsers currently support extensions, but we tried it using Quetta Browser, and it works flawlessly without any issues.
What’s Next for the Extension? (Roadmap)
This extension is primarily built with our users in mind, and also for others who are reading this post. We are not hosting it on the Google Chrome Web Store, and direct updates will be shared through this blog post and direct download links from the product page.
You can directly download it from this webpage, and if you want the latest ones, we will notify you on our social media channels. Also, there are two more features in the timeline. One is for the desktop to show a table of contents, so that it would be easy for the user to jump to a specific section immediately. And also, planning for a better speech-to-text future.
One noticeable downside of using this extension is that not every web page works the same. Sometimes the extension may not work as expected on websites that contain text in a different format. However, we have optimized this extension for most of these cases to handle the text without any issues.
And we also don’t want to hurt publisher revenue, including ours. We are looking for a way to not remove ads by publishers without affecting the users’ reading experience.
So that is all about the extension, and it is free for anybody to download and install on their device. If you have any feedback, you can share it in the comments below.
How to install and use the Luma Reader extension on desktop or mobile?
Since the extension is not hosted on the Google Web Store, you need to manually add it to your extensions. The process is very simple. Download the ZIP file of the extension (preferably the latest version) and extract it. You will get an extension folder. Open Google Chrome, go to Extensions, and enable Developer mode.
Next, tap on “Load unpacked” and select the folder, and that’s it. The extension will be added to your browser. To use it on mobile, you can use Quetta browser (download) and follow the same process. To help you understand better, here is a detailed video on how to install and use it.
